SUSPECTED ARMED HIGHWAY ROBBERY ON BRENNAN ROAD, OOL.
At 12.40 a.m. 31-1-40, one Foo Seu Wah (胡善華)
chauffeur No.134 of Silver Taxi Co., (Driving Permit
No. 17549), reported that at 11.30 p.m. 30-1-40, he
answered a call, driving car Lic.No.18266, from the
Avenue Rd. Silver Taxi Station to the Nyi Wa (藝華)
Motion Picture Co., Connaught Road. When he arrived
there five men came out of the premises and boarded his
car. They told him to drive to Jesfield Park and when
his car arrived at Brennan Road, about 200 yards south
of Jesfield Brennan Piece, four men, all dressed in
Chinese short jacket and pants, stood in the road and
barred his way. One of them had a torch which he shone
in the drivers face and waved the car to a standstill.
The driver stopped his car and one of the men
approached the car and it was seen he had a small
black pistol in his hand. He opened the door of the
car and told the five men to alight. They did so and
the three other men searched them. When they had
concluded their search they told the passengers to get
back into the car. Whilst they were doing so, several
persons passed by the car and the robbers appeared to
become alarmed and walked away.
The passengers told the chauffeur to drive on to
Jesfield Park, which he did.

Misc.No.63/40.
1/2.

Arriving at the Jessfield Park, they told the
car to stop and one of the passengers alighted. The
remaining four told the chauffeur to drive to 8te.
F. Destelen, and on arrival there a second passenger
alighted. The chauffeur was then told to drive to
Rue Prelupt where the remaining three left the car.
The chauffeur cannot say whether anything was
stolen or give any useful description of the culprits,
apart from the fact they spoke Kiangsu dialect.
The passengers did not appear to be unduly
disturbed by their experience and advised the chauffeur
not to bother to report the matter to the station.

Report on Shooting Affray.
S.C.G.P.B.

At 9.50p.m. 6/3/40, a telephone message was received
at the station reporting that a shooting affray had taken
place on Jessfield Road near Connaught Road.

A party of police under S.T. Daintery attended.

Enquiries made by D.S. Meeks, D.C.I. Yao Yuen Loong
and C.D.C. 147 ascertained that at about 9.40p.m. 6/3/40,
a plain-clothes search party, believed to be from 76
Jessfield Road, were operating in lane 119 Jessfield Road
(Chinese No. 776), when they encountered three male
Chinese, who on being challenged, opened fire on the
search party, who turned the fire.

No person was injured, but one male Chinese was
arrested.

The S.M. Police party made a search on the roadway
and succeeded in finding two misfire 7.65 cartridges, two
7.65 cartridge cases and two .380 cartridge cases. These
are being forwarded to the A.I.S. for examination.

Enquiries at the S.C.G.P.B. Headquarters, 13 Jess-
field Road revealed that they were unable to supply the
arrested man's name and address etc., as he had been
taken to 76 Jessfield Road.

Forwarded for information.

Sen.Det./C.
D. S. 252.

At 3.54 a.m. 9/2/40 a telephone message was received from C.P.C. 1176 of the French Police stating that he was detaining a motor car at Weihaiwei and Mohawk Roads corner. P.S. Egberg attended and brought both chauffeur and Policeman to the Station.
Enquiries in the Charge-Room showed that motor car license No. 1375 driven by Yao Ts Hyi (姚智喜) License no. 1135 of 76 Jessfield Road was challenged by C.P.C. 1176 while travelling East to West on Ave. Ed. VII. It failed to stop immediately, the French C.P.C. blew his whistle and gave chase and the car stopped on Racecourse Road outside the Racecourse Apartments. Chauffeur handed over to the French Police at 4.35 a.m. 9/2/40 on instructions of D.O. "A" Div.
The motor car was taken away at 8.30 a.m. 9/2/40 from Weihaiwei and Mohawk Roads corner by the French Police.

It is reported that on 20 Dec (王永發 alias Sai Fah or 亡百章) was shot and killed on Bubbling Well Road a few days ago on the instigation of Wang and his co-conspirator Tsoo Tsui (夏越) was taken into custody, and is now being held as prisoner at 7C.

1.

ARREST OF MEMBERS OF SPECIAL PEACE PRESERVA-
TION CORPS (巡衛隊) AFFILIATED TO THE
SPECIAL BRANCH OF WANG CHING WEI'S (汪精衛)
PARTY, 76 JESSFIELD RD.

At 10.10 p.m. 23/10/39, I.P.C.s 973, 1008, 1552,
1454 and 290 on duty Traffic Post duty at the inter-
section of Jessfield Road and Tifeng Road, brought to
the station a male Chinese named Hu Zang Tsing (胡長情),
22, Anhwei, residing 35 Edinburgh Road.

At 10.25 p.m. 23/10 39, the above I.P.C.s brought
to the station two other male Chinese Sze Tse Tsing
(施志清), 26, Tsungming. Sung Zau Liang (沈兆良),
20, Tsungming, both residing 35 Edinburgh Road.

The I.P.C.s stated, that whilst on duty at the
above place they observed the above Chinese who were
riding bicycles riding up and down Jessfield Road. As
their actions appeared to be very suspicious and, the
fact that they stated they were on patrol in that sec-
tion in connection with the above named Association,
they brought them to the station for further enquiries.

A search ascertained that the men were unarmed.

Questioned by D.S. Till, I.D.S.273, I.D.C.s 279
and 314 the following was ascertained:-

The men stated that they were employed by the
above Association, 76 Jessfield Road, but were attached
to a sub-branch situated at 35 Edinburgh Road under the

Misc.No.537 39

1/2.

command of one named Lee Pang An (李邦安).
They were part of a contingent of 60 male Chinese,
who resided on the premises, a number of whom were armed
with Mauser and small pistols (approximately 16). Only
those who were unarmed participated in patrol work, the
remainder armed, were confined to guard duties inside
the premises.
All members had been recruited during the past
few months after their antecedents had been carefully
investigated. One week ago all members had been supplied
with a blue cotton cloth uniforms,fashioned on the style
of Dr. Sun Yat Sen.
The monthly salary of the members ranged from
$30.00 to $75.0 , according to ability and length of
service.
The patrol duties were commenced on the 21/10 39,
and all unarmed members were allocated to various beats
in the vicinity of 76 Jessfield Road. In this respect
the arrested members were on bicycle patrol duty between
35 Edinburgh Road, Kinnear Road and Jessfield and Tifen
Road. Their hours of duty consisted of 3 hour shifts,
between 6 a.m. to 12 m.n. When arrested they were on
duty from 9 p.m. to 12 m.n.
During their off duty periods, no members were
allowed to leave the premises, food being supplied on

Misc.No.587 39
1/5.

a monthly payment of $10.00.
The object of these patrols were to observe the
movements of any suspicious persons or any unusual
occurrence. Upon such person s being detected, two were
instructed to keep the person/s in sight, whilst the
other immediately reported the matter to 35 Edinburgh
Road.
Upon receipt of the information a small detachment
would be dispatched and the suspicious person/s would be
arrested and taken to 35 Edinburgh Road for enquiries.
The arrested men were finger printed, but investi-
gation showed that all had no previous record.
Mr. Tabrum, A.D.D.C. "B" was informed who attended
the station. After being acquainted with all particulars,
he gave instructions that the men be released. Acting
accordingly, they were allowed to go at 12 m.n.
Statements attached.

ILLEGAL FUNCTIONING OF THE "SELF DEFENSE CORPS"

At 7.20 p.m. 19/10/39 a telephone message was
received from Tsih Lien Liang (戚善良) reporting that
his father had returned home.

The undersigned accompanied by C.D.S.167 proceeded
to 84 Edinburgh Road and interviewed Tsih Lai Kung who
stated that he had been kept all the time at 21 Mei Hwa
Li, Zau Ke Yih, where the members of the "Self Defense
Corps" handcuffed him and by beating him continuously
tried to force him to agree to pay compensation to Sung
Zung Fah, who was also present there.

When their attempts failed they told Tsih Lai Kung
that he could be released on payment of "fine" in the sum
of $600.00 or producing a guarantee that the above "fine"
would be paid in the nearest future. Being unable to
stand the torture, Tsih Lai Kung agreed to pay the "fine"
and produced a guarantor, after which he was released at
about 7 p.m. 19/10/39.

1.

ILLEGAL FUNCTIONING OF THE "SELF DEFENSE CORPS"

At 11.40 a.m. 19/10/39 Tsih Zien Liang (戚善良)
of 84/86 Edinburgh Road, C.C.L., reported to the Central
Station that his father Tsih Lai Kung (戚来根), 57,
Ningpo, building contractor, had been abducted by several
armed men from the above address at about 9.30 a.m. even
date. As the alleged offence was committed in this
district, the complt. was sent with C.D.S.185 to this
station.

Further enquiries have been made by D.S.I.
Golenbkoff, D.S.I. Yao Yuen Loong and C.D.S.167 and
the following facts were ascertained:-

Tsih Lai Kung about 2 months ago signed a contract
with the Topas Land Investment, 102 Central Arcade for
the construction of a block of houses in the French
Concession. Previously this contract was in the hands
of a contractor Sung Zung Foh (孫順福), but was with-
drawn by the Topas Land Investment Co., owing to unsatis-
factory work, and given to Tsih Lai Kung. Sung Zung
Foh was very much irritated and blamed Tsih Lai Kung
for the loss of the contract. He anticipated a profit
of about $50,000.00 and lately approached Tsih Lai Kung
and demanded from him the sum of $20,000.00 as compensa-
tion. Tsih Lai Kung refused to pay any compensation, as
according to the contract all claims of Sung Zung Foh

Miss.No.583/39

1/2.

were to be addressed to the Topas Land Investment Co.,
Sung Zung Poh, however, pressed his demands against
Tsih Lai Kung and recently threatened to cause harm to
the last named.
At about 9.30 a.m. 19/10/39, Tsih Lai Kung was in
his room at 84 Edinburgh Road when suddenly 6 or 7 men
in plain clothes entered the house via open door, four
of them produced pistols and ordered Tsih Lai Kung to
accompany them.
They led him to the road where they called a
private ricksha No. 2915, pulled by coolie Zung Ah
Poh (陳阿福), badge No.4240, which was waiting nearby
for his passenger and placed the victim on the footboard
whilst one of the armed men sat in the ricksha. Then the
above coolie was ordered to pull the ricksha south along
Edinburgh Road, the other men following them on foot.
When the party was near Lucern Road, the victim
began to shout for help, whereupon the armed men pulled
him off the ricksha and forced to walk with them, whilst
the ricksha was ordered to go away.
At about 12 noon a male Chinese riding a bicycle
arrived at the victim's home and stated that Tsih Lai
Kung was detained at the office of the 7th company of
the "Self Defense Corps" in zau ka yih (曹家堰) village
off Edinburgh Road. (This organization forms the subject

Miss.No.583/32

1/3.

of the information report forwarded by Sen. Det. i/c.
B.W. on 29/8/39). The messenger said that Tsih Lai Kung
requested the documents relating to the contract to be
sent to him, and produced Tsih LAI KUNG's card on which
the latter wrote himself a message to his family. The
photographs of the documents were sent by the victim's
son in law with their servant Lee Hoong Tsing (李鴻清)
who accompanied the messenger. The servant was led to
house No. 21, Mei Hwa Li (美華里), Zau Ka Yih off Edin-
burgh Road, where he saw Tsih Lai Kung surrounded by a
large number of the members of the "Self Defense Corps".
The photographs were taken from the servant and he was
ordered to return home.

The houses Nos. 84 & 86 Edinburgh Road are situated
in the lane known as Moon Villa, about 40 yards off Edin-
burgh Road and S.M.C. taxes are being paid by the occu-
pants.

Sir,
It is reported that premises No. 199 Fung Wah Road,
Pah Tha Village are occupied by one Sung Tsung Mei (沈忠美)
a lieutenant of Lee Shih Chun (李自群), this man has a
following of 30 men who are armed with 40 mausers and have
a number of grenades stored in the premises.
They style themselves the Pah Hwa Kyau Tsah Dai
(巡察隊) "Investigation Corps" and are under the direct
control of Lee Shih Chun, who details them for any special
work he may require carried out.
A country style house in the Loo Sin Zah (錫宅)
Village is occupied by some 150 men all natives of Anhwei,
who are armed with 60 pistols of various types, these
pistols having been obtained by the men themselves from
unknown sources, they are in charge of one named Too Luh
San (胡德山), well known Tau Ka Woo loafer and style
themselves the Tze Wei Dai (自衛隊), "Self Defence Corps"
These men are taught each day by a member of the
Japanese Gendarmerie on military and political subjects,
these men are under Japanese control and not connected with
Lee Shih Chun.
Houses No. 6 & 7, Lane 95 Edinburgh Road are
occupied by some 36 unarmed men who were brought to
Shanghai from Tsungkang, Tsungkong, they are in charge of
one named Sung Ching Meu (沈金茂), who is assisted by
one Bah Dah Loong (白大龍), these men were formerly
guerrillas in their native districts and were driven out
by a stronger band, so took refugee in Shanghai under
Japanese control.

Sir;

Regarding certain information given to Mr. Sanson,
Assistant Commissioner, by Major Ashmore, Brigade Major,
British Force, I have to report the following:-

At 2.30 p.m. Sept. 20, 1939 Mr. R. Wright,
President of the Theosophical Society at 75 Jessfield
Road which is situated opposite to and overlooks the
grounds of No.76, came to Bubbling Well Station and
stated as follows:-

At about noon of Sept. 15, 1939 a representative of
76 called at 75 and informed the Chinese servants of
their desire to occupy the building for office purposes,
and requested that an interview be arranged with some
responsible person connected with the Theosophical
Society. As a result of this request an interview was
arranged between the President of the Society, Mr. R.
Wright, and representatives of 76 at 4 p.m. Sept. 15.

At this interview which was held at 75 Jessfield
Road, there were present two representatives of 76. One
appeared to be a Japanese who spoke English and Chinese
fluently, and acted as interpreter to the Chinese
representative during the talk. Mr. H.B. Campbell, an
American citizen and Paint merchant, was present in an
advisory capacity to the Society. The lessee of the
house is an American citizen named A.P. Knudsen.

The representatives of 76 opened the conversation
by expressing a desire to rent the building. They were
informed that the building had been leased for a period
of 10 years and that the Society had expended a consider-

able amount of money in adopting the premises to its
needs. The representatives of 76 asked for details of
expenditure and were informed that it was about $20,000.
After considerable discussion the representatives of 76
expressed a desire that a detailed list of expenditure
be furnished them. With this end in view a further
meeting was arranged for Friday, Sept. 22, 1939.
The representatives of 76 were informed that the
Society would be unable to vacate the premises for at
least one month, even if requirements for transfer of

interest to note that due to the location of 75
Jessfield Road persons entering and leaving are always

searchlight onto the windows of 75, evidently for the
purpose of spotting persons who may be spying.

At 8:30 A.M., September 13, 1939., the
two workers of the Foh Loong Silk Filature, No.957
Kiaochow Road, O.O.L., namely, Tseu Tuh Foh (周德福),
and Kwok Siau Mau (郭小毛), who had been arrested at the
above factory by the Chinese Volunteer Corps on 10.9.39.,
came to the Station and reported that they had been
released on 11.9.39.

It appears that they were arrested by the
Special Service Squad of the Chinese Volunteer Corps,
(中華自衛團特務部), stationed at No.1 Kong Ka Jau, off
Jessfield Road, O.O.L., at the request of Ah Sze (阿四),
an ex-worker of the Foh Loong Silk Filature, who accused
them of having been concerned together in stealing his
gold finger ring and other property from his quarters
on the factory premises, whilst he was being employed there

Following their arrest, they were taken
to No.1 Kong Ka Jau, off Jessfield Road, O.O.L., where
they were detained in a ground floor rear room, which is
protected with iron grill gates and gives the appearance
of a prison.

whilst C.I.C.2364 and himself took cover in a shop

Sir,

    I beg to report that at about 3.35p.m. 2-7-39,
whilst on search party with C.P.C.s 2364, 2564 and 2989,
and female searcher Zung Zee Sz No. 32 on Edinburgh Road
between Yu Yuen Road and Avenue Haig, I observed three
male Chinese, dressed in civilian clothes, coming out of
a lane situated on the West-side of Edinburgh Road and
about 100 yards South of Yu Yuen Road.

    I ordered the C. P.C.s to search the men, which they
did, and then allowed the men to go. They crossed the
road and walked into Lane 95 Edinburgh Road.

    A few minutes later, I saw one of the men standing
at the mouth of the lane and pointing a pistol at us in
a threatening manner.

    I immediately ordered the search party to take
shelter in shop doors, which they did. As we entered
various shops, some person fired several shots along the
road from the direction of Lane 95 Edinburgh Road. I did
not see who fired these shots. I then shouted to C.P.C.
2564 to telephone the station, and as he was leaving
the shop, where he had taken cover, a uniform S.C.G.P.B.
Policeman, who had joined the three plainclothes men, at
the mouth of Lane 95, lifted his rifle to his shoulder
and fired two or three shots at C.P.C. 2564 as he ran
along Edinburgh Road towards Yu Yuen Road.

    On arriving at Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads inter-
section, C.P.C. 2564 found that C.P.C. 3021, off duty,
had learned the shooting and had already informed the
Station by street telephone. He was then joined by C.P.C.
2989 who ran along Edinburgh Road after him.

C.P.C. 2364 and myself, who meanwhile had taken
cover in a shop No. 508 Edinburgh Road, were suddenly
surprised by two other plainclothes Chinese, both armed
with mausers, who had worked their way through various
lanes to the rear of the shop, and who ordered us to
drop our pistols.
Realizing that we were out numbered, I did not
open fire, but only kept the men covered.
One of them then fired one shot, which went over my
head and lodged in the wall of the shop. Both of them then
jumped back out of my sight.
C.P.C. 2364 shouted to them to stop firing. At
this point a male Chinese of small stature dressed in
a light fown jacket and khaki shorts, ran out of the lane
on the west side of the road, and ordered our attackers
to stop firing. He then shouted to me in English and
asked me not to fire.
I came out of the shop and stood at his side, and

road, I asked him if he would accompany me to the Station.
He refused, and leaving us, he walked back in the
direction of Lane 95 Edinburgh Road.
The C.P.C. and myself continued toward Yu Yuen Road,
and waited at the corner of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads
for the party from the Station, who arrived about two
minutes later.

ARREST OF C.D.C. 279 BY ARMED MEMBERS
OF TIH SUH CHUNG (鐵血軍).
========================================

For the purpose of verifying an address given by
a suspect in a larceny case brought to the Bubbling Well
Station by C.P.C. 1385 at 6.15 a.m. June 22, 1939.
C.D.C.279 was despatched by D.S. 252 Weeks to Lane 1423,
House 5, Yu Yuen Road.

The C.D.C. proceeded by station car and alighted
at the entrance to the alleyway. He was looking for
the number of the alleyway standing on the Yu Yuen Road
footpath when two male Chinese, who were standing at the
entrance to the alleyway suddenly threatened him with
mauser pistols. The detective thinking they were
highway robbers offered them money. The suspected
robbers pulled the detective into the alleyway and there
searched him and upon finding that he was armed accused
him of being a traitor. At this juncture the two
suspects were re-enforced by about 20 other armed men.
The C.D.C. was subjected to interrogation and then
marched away to a Chinese style house in the Zau Ka Yi
village situated between Edinburgh and Great Western
Roads.

At 8.05 a.m. June 22, Inspector Yee Kyin Kwei
received a telephone message from Lee Shih Chung (李自群)
living at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road, C.C.L.

Misc.No.335/39.
1/2.

informing the Inspector that a detective attached to
Bubbling Well Station had been arrested by a gang of men
and he would effect the release of the detective as a
mistake had been made.
In consequence of this message D.I. Fabrum, Insp.
Yao Kyu, Kwei and D.S. Weeks promptly proceeded to Lane
95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
Upon arrival at the Lane leading to this house,
the Police party noticed several armed men standing in
the alleyway. Evidently the Police party were expected
as the iron door leading to the compound of the house
was promptly opened to admit them.
Upon entering the compound, the Police were confron-
ted by about 30 men all armed with mauser pistols. The
gate-keeper was armed with a mauser fitted with an
automatic stock.
The Police party were escorted to a large room on
the ground-floor. They were received in a very friendly
manner by Lee Shih Chung who introduced the 10 or 12
men present, some of whom were armed. Included in those
introduced were Sung Tsong Mei (沈忠美), Zee Wen Can
(徐文安), a Mr. Chu and one named Lee Yin Fei (李飛).
The last named, according to information of Bubbling
Well detectives was shot by Inspector Dudley and D.S.I.
Filten when participating in an Armed Robbery at No.8

Misc.No. 335/39.

1/3.

Fan Wah Sing Tsung off Rockhill Avenue, Misc.No. 297/39
(BW) and later removed to Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh
Road in Lee Shih Chung's M/car. During the discussion
Lee Yih Fei openly admitted being shot three times
and showed the Police the scars on his body resulting
from the bullet wounds he received. He was shot twice
in the back and once in the buttocks.

    Lee Shih Chung who was previously unknown to any
of the visiting Police is a man of small stature, aged
about 35/6. He claims to be the owner of a steamship
line and also the owner of a Native Bank on Kiukiang
Road. He is a loquacious talker and desires to give
the impression that he is a man of great power. In
response to many questions concerning himself and the
numerous armed men surrounding him, he stated in
principle, that he had was a man of such power that he
was not subject either to the rule of the Japanese
or members of the Shanghai City Government. He had
under him between 700 or 800 men, most of whom, he
stated had been recruited from the villages in the
Western Area of Shanghai. This organization, he
called the Tih Suh Chung (Iron Colour Corps) (鐵血軍)
50 of whom act as bodyguards to himself.

"B"
Misc.No.335/39.
1/4.

Questioned as to the expenses for the upkeep of
this organization, Lee stated they are at present
poorly supported but when they need funds he provides
them.
The object of this organization, Lee stated, is
to eliminate members of pro-Chinese assassination
groups. Lee even went so far as to say that C.D.C.279 would
have been executed if it had not have been for the
fact that he was able to establish his identity by virtue
of the fact that he had a S.M.P. Warrant Card and S.M.P.
pistol and was later proved to be a member of the S.M.P.
Lee proposed that his organization be accorded
friendly treatment by detectives at Bubbling Well
Station with whom he expressed a desire to co-operate
for the specific purpose of exterminating members of
pro-Chinese assassination groups. He further stated
that as Police at Bubbling Well Station were responsible
for law and order in territory under the jurisdiction
of the S.M.C. in the Western Area that he be afforded
all possible protection.
Lee concluded the discussion which had lasted more
than one hour by stating that within a month or two
from now Mr. Wang Ching Wei would probably come to
Shanghai and there would be peace and quietness in the
Western Area of Shanghai.

Misc.No.335/39.
1/8.

During the discussion Sergeant Major Shida
entered the room, he was greeted in a friendly manner
by all. He left after a few minutes, not knowing the
reason for presence of the S.M.P. Lee stated as he was
not obliged to tell Sergeant Major Shida, whom he would
not inform of the incident.

Some of the men the Police saw and were introduced
to at Lee's residence were students between 20 and 25
years of age. Others were of the robber and loafer type.

The C.D.C. was handed over to D.I. Tabrum together
with his pistol and Warrant Card at about 10.15a.m.
With the exception of being scared the detective had
not been injured in anyway.

After returning to the Station, Inspector
Yamaguchi approached D.I. Tabrum and asked if there had
been any trouble at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
He explained that Sergeant Major Shida had just phoned
for information and stated that to approach this
particular house was very dangerous and, that he had
received instructions from a high authority to cause
the arrest of all unauthorized persons found in the

Wang's "Merry Men"
Special Police
Make Debut In

Causing a mild flurry of uneasiness at their first appearance, when residents feared that they might function in the Western area, nearly 1,300 recruits of the Nanking Government's special police donned their new green uniforms for the first time yesterday, after undergoing a period of training at the Hollywood Gardens on Yu Yuen Road, former gambling den closed down a few months ago by order of the Shanghai Special Municipality.

MAR 6 1940
9236
26 4 40

A Test Case
THE local organ of Japanese opinion, the Shanghai Mainichi, can usually be trusted to put its feet into it, if there is the slightest opportunity for so doing. The latest example of the penchant followed the arrest by a detachment of the British Defense Force, of a party of Chinese gun-men, in a lane off Crescent Alley, inside the British Defense Sector. The British troops stopped and searched a couple of suspicious looking Chinese, and found that both of them were armed with Mauser pistols. They then surrounded the headquarters of the gang, and called upon the inmates to surrender. Eleven men came out, and a search of the premises led to the seizure of seven more pistols. After this coup Japanese Gendarmes appeared on the scene, and demanded that the seized weapons should be handed over to them. This demand was rejected by the British Military authorities, who intimated that the men and their weapons would only be released when they had been identified by some responsible organization, and their presence, armed, in the British Sector was satisfactorily explained.

The significance of the Japanese demand for the handing over of the nine pistols became apparent a few days later. But in the interval the Shanghai Mainichi put both feet into it by printing an article attacking the British troops for "unruly conduct" in arresting and detaining "20 Chinese workers of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's organization." Such "outrageous acts" required the punishment of the "British Tommies," and were especially to be deplored, following as they did upon the signature of an agreement for the policing of the Western Roads area.

THE admission that the men arrested by the British troops were "workers of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's organization" is likely to have most embarrassing consequences for the Japanese authorities, especially their Gendarmerie and Special Service Section. It has repeatedly been alleged by the Municipal Police and as frequently denied by the Japanese military, that most of the outrages committed within the Settlement during the past few months by pro-Japanese Gangsters, were perpetrated by proteges of Mr. Wang Ching-wei and the Special Service Section. If the demand of the Japanese Gendarmerie in this instance had been complied with the evidence connecting Mr. Wang Ching-wei's workers with these crimes would certainly have vanished. Fortunately, the British military retained the weapons, and placed them at the disposal of the Ballistics experts of the S. M. Police for investigation.

Now the science of identifying fire-arms has attained such perfection, that given empty cartridge cases, or a not too deformed bullet, the weapon from which it has been fired can be identified with the same certainty as a finger-print record. As the result of the "unruly conduct" of the British Tommies, this is what the Police discovered:

Among the weapons seized were three pistols which were used in the murderous attack upon the offices of the China Evening News on the evening of July 22, 1939, during which an American citizen, Mr. "Tug" Wilson was murdered; they also included the pistols used in an affray at the Asia Club, 65, Gordon Road, on September 11, 1938; in a battle with the S. M. Police in Sinza Road on July 21, 1939; in the murder of a Chinese Constable and the wounding of a Sikh at the traffic control at the corner of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads on October 10, 1939; in an armed robbery in Robison Road on June 20, 1939; in an outrage on the premises of the University Press in Ningpo Road on June 17, 1939; in armed robberies in Singapore Road in June 1939; in an attack upon a mounted Sikh Patrol on Jessfield Road on June 15, 1939; in another armed robbery in Taku Road on May 23, 1939; and finally in a murderous attack upon two Sikh Police in Jessfield Road on June 27, 1939. It would appear, then that these "workers of Mr. Wang Ching-wei's organization" are in fact a gang of armed desperadoes, some of whom at least merit the death sentence, and others long terms of imprisonment.

IT will be interesting to see what attitude is taken by the Japanese Military authorities, now that the connection between these men, and a long series of armed outrages, including several murders, has been definitely established. Will they cooperate in seeing that the men are brought to trial, and punished as they deserve, or will they—as has occurred on previous occasions—demand that they be handed over in order that they may be permitted to escape? It seems to be a test case. The evidence of the S.M.P. Ballistic experts is conclusive. The onus of proving that they did not use the weapons found in their possession for the crimes committed with them, rests squarely upon the shoulders of the arrested men. It would be asking us to stretch our imagination beyond breaking point to believe that the pistols came into their possession innocently, after all these outrages had been perpetrated. The Shanghai Mainichi's angry diatribe against the British troops, however, has placed the Japanese in a most embarrassing position. It appears to make it necessary for them, if they value their prestige, definitely to repudiate any connection between the arrested men and Mr. Wang's organization. It must be regarded as out of the question for the Japanese military to extend their protection to a gang of armed desperadoes with such an appalling record. Obviously, their best course would be to cooperate with the S.M.Police in seeing that these men get their just deserts. The possibility of treating them as the injured victims of the "unruly conduct" of "British Tommies" vanished when the latter refused to part with the seized weapons except to the Ballistic experts of the S. M. Police.

OUTRAGEOUS BRITISH SOLDIERS.

At about 9 a.m. February 27, a member of Wang Ching

FEB 8 1940

British Military Nab Wang Men
Fourteen Arrested In Raid,
More Than 10 Guns Captured

Fourteen armed men attached to the Wang Ching-wei faction are in the hands of the British Military authorities as a result of quick action by a British patrol in a lane off Crescent Avenue yesterday morning.

The men were seized together with more than 10 pistols and a large quantity of ammunition, despite a demand of the Japanese Gendarmerie for custody of the weapons. This demand was later withdrawn.

Carrying out normal duty at 9:20 a.m. yesterday, a British patrol spotted two Chinese in blue gowns in a lane off Crescent Avenue, both armed with Mauser pistols.

Couple Arrested

Surrounding the couple, the tom-mies arrested them without a single shot being fired.

An immediate investigation on the spot revealed that the head-quarters of the two men was near by, and the patrol insisted that the captured men lead to it. Accordingly, the Tommies were led to a house protected by a breastwork. Encircling the building and posting guards armed with rifles and a machine-gun at all strategic points, the tommies ordered the occupants to surrender themselves. After a brief wait, no less than 12 men filed out.

A search of the premises revealed several more pistols and an ammunition cache.

Japanese Claim Arms

Before the patrol had time to leave the place a squad from the Japanese Gendarmerie arrived. They made no request for the custody of the men who, they said, were supporters of Mr. Wang Ching-wei but demanded custody of the arms and ammunition.

This request was withdrawn when it was pointed out that the British patrol was functioning well within its proper defense sector, and that the men and the weapons would be released as soon as some responsible organization identified them and explained their presence in the British sector.

The 14 men were loaded into British army trucks which arrived in the meantime, and were transported to a British barracks, where they are being detained.

saw two suspicious Chinese, wearing
long gowns, as they were about to
leave the alleyway in question. A
search of the loafers showed that they
were armed with Mauser pistols.
Questioning revealed that they were
living in a house in the same alley-
way, whereupon the British soldiers
asked to be led there.

After the soldiers had surrounded
the small house, the occupants were
ordered to come out, with the result
that eleven more men soon stood in
the alleyway with their arms in the
air. A search of the premises brought
the weapons and ammunition to light.

While a truck was being awaited to
convey the men and the seized wea-
pons to headquarters, Japanese Gen-
darmerie arrived on the scene and
requested that the weapons be turned
over to them on the grounds that the
men were connected with Mr. Wang
Ching-wei. No request was made for
the men to be handed over. Con-
versations on the spot finally led the
Japanese to desist from their request
and the men, together with their
weapons and ammunition were taken
to headquarters.

Up to a late hour last night, no
further request had been received for
the handing-over of the men or their
guns.

Gambling Dens Moving

With new gambling houses spring-
ing up like mushrooms and robberies
often reported, Nantao is being trans-
formed into the second "badlands" in
Shanghai, it being asserted that "there
are thorns in every step" in the
native city. According to the "Shun
Pao," two big gambling houses came
into existence in the native city dur-
ing the Lunar New Year period and
four others were established during
the past few days.

A few others will soon be establish-
ed and they have even put up adver-
tisements to invite customers. These
new ones are going to be pure gam-
bling houses where waitresses will
work also. A Chinese Theatre in
Oong Ka Loong has been transformed
into a gambling den known as Hsieh
Lee.

Gangsters who formerly worked in
similar establishments in the western
district have come to Nantao in large
numbers and as a result, highway
hold-ups are reported often, the re-
port states.

FEB 2 / 1940

Wang Ching-wei Men
Raided In Hide-Out

PAIR OF BANDITS
ORDERED TO LEAD
TROOPS TO HOUSE

Japanese Gendarmes Withdraw First Demand
For Custody Of Arms, Ammunition;
Gunmen Taken To Barracks

Soldiers Surround Barricaded Lair

Raiding a lair in the badlands this morning, British troops arrested 12 Wang Ching-wei supporters and seized their arms and ammunition, after the soldiers had first surprised two others of the gang.

All fourteen, with a considerable number of pistols, are now in the custody of the British forces, despite an earlier request by Japanese military gendarmes that they should be allowed to take the arms

Crescent Avenue
Out on its usual round, a patrol of British troops about 9.20 a.m. surprised two Chinese loafers in blue gowns, down an alleyway off Crescent Avenue. Both men were armed with Mausers.

Going into action swiftly, the soldiers arrested the two and disarmed them before they had any chance to do any damage.

Further Search
The troops were not content with just arresting the pair. They decided on a further search, and ordered the Chinese couple to lead them to their headquarters.

With rifles and a machinegun at the ready, the patrol followed the Chinese. The trail led to a Chinese house not far off, protected by a breastwork.

House Raided
Covering the house from strategic points, the British tom-mies ordered its occupants to come out. They totalled no less than a dozen. Then a search was made of the place, and several pistols and a pile of ammunition was discovered.

A few minutes later Japanese military gendarmes arrived on the scene. They demanded that they be given custody of the arms, as the men were supporters of Wang Ching-wei. They made no request for the custody of the men.

Objection Withdrawn
There was then a certain amount of discussion, following which the Japanese withdrew their objection to the British troops (who were functioning in their own proper defense sector) from taking the arms and ammunition.

British army trucks arrived near the scene, and the fourteen gangsters and their equipment were removed to a British army barracks, where they are being detained.

Pistols Seized By East No. S. B D. 6
Surreys Have Records Of
Crime And Terror In City

Three Guns Had Been Used During The Attack On
Press Row In Avenue Edward VII; Weapons
Belong To Group Responsible For Murders

THIRTEEN MEN SEIZED ON TUESDAY
STILL HELD BY BRITISH MILITARY

A most sensational record of armed crime and terrorism
in the International Settlement and along the Outside Roads,
dating right back to November, 1938, has been linked up by
the Shanghai Municipal Police following the seizure of nine
pistols on Tuesday morning by a patrol of the East Surrey
Regiment from a gang of armed gangsters in the Western Area.
Ballistic experts have definitely established that three of
the guns seized from the 13 men arrested on Tuesday, were
used in the bloody attack by armed terrorists on the offices of
the "China Evening News" at 160 Avenue Edward VII, in "The
Shanghai Times" Building on the night of July 22 last, during
which Mr. F. A. "Tug" Wilson, an American, was killed and 13
Chinese wounded, including three policemen.

Ballistic experts have further
pointed out that the nine guns
seized by the British military from
the Chinese, who are now being
held in custody, belong to a group
of 20 weapons, six of which have
already been seized. The records
of the guns show that they had
been used on various occasions to
murder and attempt to murder
officers of the Shanghai Municipal
Policy, as well as in armed rob-
beries and intimidation attempts.
The fact that the nine guns have
been seized from the 13 arrested
men does not necessarily indicate
that they had been implicated in
all or in part of the various acts
of terrorism, murder and armed
crime in which the pistols had
been used, but leads to the belief
that all the terrorism had been
directed from areas outside the
Settlement.

13 Men Still Held
Despite the announcement by
the British Military that the 13
men would be handed over to
any bona fide authorities, who came
to claim them, or, made a suitable
explanation, up to last night no one
came to claim the men or spoke
on their behalf. Up to the present
it is not known whether the men
themselves have revealed anything
or whether they had been question-
ed at all.
It will be recalled that the East
Surreys patrol seized two suspi-
cious-looking Chinese off Crescent
Avenue near Yu Yuen Road on
Tuesday morning and found two
pistols on them. Later the men
led the British Military to a village
near-by, where in a house the
soldiers seized 11 more men and
seven guns, all were taken off to
the British Military headquarters
despite protests of Japanese Gen-
darmerie, who asked that the seiz-
ed weapons be given to them.
The East Surreys seized in all
four Mauser pistols and five wea-
pons of other makes as follows:
Mauser 7.63 pistol No. 892708
Mauser 7.63 pistol No. 890582
Mauser 7.63 pistol No. 713255
Mauser 7.63 pistol No. 1749
Astra 7.63 pistol No. 6396
Royal 7.63 pistol No. 19376
Demon .32 pistol No. 88256
Francais .32 pistol No. 2715
Im. Browning .32 pistol No. 2034

Of these nine pistols Mausers
892708 and 1749 and the Astra 6396
were used by the large gang of
terrorists in the attack on "News-
paper Row" on July 22, last, when
bombs were thrown and a large
number of shots were fired, creat-
ing a panic all over the city.

Killing Of Policeman
The other six guns seized, the
Arms Identification Bureau of the
S.M.P. has established, were used
in the brutal killing of Chinese Con-
stable No. 3378 of the S.M.P., on
the night of November 20, last,
whilst he was on duty at the cor-
ner of Edinburgh and Yu Yuen
Roads. Sikh Constable 459 was
seriously wounded at the time. The
shooting created, it will be recalled,
serious tension in the western area,
and was referred to as the most
cowardly attack upon the officers
of the law. There did not appear
to be any motive for this cowardly
affair other than the intimidation of
members of the Shanghai Municip-
al Police, it was contended at the
time.
The general attacks on members
of the Shanghai Municipal Police
along Outside Roads during the
whole of last year is included in
the records of the seized guns. The
guns were used on June 27, last,
in the attempt to murder two Sikh
constables outside 1,464 Jessfield
Road, as well as the attempted
murder of two other Sikh con-
stables whilst they were on patrol
on Jessfield Road at 11.20 a.m. on
June 15, last. A shooting affray
ensued at the time, the gunmen
firing 20 shots and escaping. The
constables were not injured.

Armed Robberies
Some of the guns belong to a
group that were used in a number
of armed robberies in the Settle-
ment, including the shooting affray
between an armed gang and a
Police Search Party on Stone
Bridge and Sinza Road on the early
morning of July 21, which resulted
in two members of the gang being
shot dead and another wounded.
Among other crimes generally
connected with the same group is

the attempted armed robbery in
Lane 506, House 69, Taku Road, a
dry cleaning shop on May 25, last,
when a shot was fired by an armed
robber when an alarm was raised,
also the armed robbery staged at
436-438 Robinson Road, on June 20,
last when four shots were fired by
the armed men upon decamping
from premises when an alarm was
raised. One shot was fired from the
same group of guns by a gunman
following a hold-up on a cotton
mill on June 15, last, at Lane 255,
Huse 101, Singapore Road.

Opium Dealer Killed
A gun from the same group was
used in the murder of an opium
hong proprietor in the Outside
Area off Brenan Road on the
evening of August 10 last. At the
time it was believed that the kill-
ing was the result of competition.
Among the earlier cases in
which certain of the same group of
weapons were used was on the
night of November 9, 1938, when
a hand grenade was thrown and a
number of shots fired in the
grounds of 65 Gordon Road, known
as the Asia Club, a gambling den.
At the time of the throwing of the
grenades a party was in progress
to celebrate the engagement of a
Korean and a Chinese lady.

Intimidation Attempt
Among the various intimidation
attempts and attacks on newspapers
the same group of weapons was
used in the attempt to intimidate
the employees of the "University
Press" at 130 Ningpo Road on the
night of June 17 last, when a num-
ber of shots were fired and a
grenade of the potato masher type
was left outside the premises.
Late yesterday it was not known
what action the British military
were going to take in connection
with the 13 men they have in
custody and whether a detailed
questioning of them would be com-
menced in order to elicit from them
information which may lead to the
arrest of others and perhaps clear
up a number of terroristic acts,
murders and armed robberies car-
ried out last year.

Reign of Terror
Traced to Set
Of Pistols

Guns Taken by British
Soldiers Here Linked
With Gory Annals

Police investigation yesterday established that some of the firearms seized by members of the East Surrey Regiment when they rounded up a gang of Chinese desperadoes in the "badlands" last Tuesday morning, had figured in an important political shooting in Shanghai last summer and that the weapons belonged to a group items of which had been used in a long series of outrages—political, anti-Police, and in connection with robberies—throughout the city but particularly in the lawless western area.

A British military patrol composed of a lance-corporal and five men arrested thirteen suspects on Tuesday in an alleyway off Crescent Avenue. They seized from the gang a rifle, eight pistols of various descriptions, and an imitation pistol. There were four Mausers, a Royal, an Astra, a Demon and a Francais pistol. All the weapons were turned over to the S.M.P. ballistics section for tests, with startling results.

The gun experts discovered that two of the Mausers and the Astra had been used in the attack by heavily-armed terrorists on a Chinese-American newspaper office in a lane skirting 160 Avenue Edward VII last July 22. The gang, whose members were later identified with a pro-Wang Ching-wei organization, threw hand-grenades and fired salvoes of pistol shots. They killed Capt. A. F. "Tug" Wilson, an American citizen, who courageously attempted to help the Police, murdered a handcart coolie who chanced to get in their way, and wounded about a dozen others, including three Chinese policemen.

Black Record of Group

In addition, examination of the weapons has established the fact that they belong to a group of twenty guns responsible for a consistent reign of terror here in 1938 and 1939.

Items in this large collection of firearms, other than those confiscated —without the shedding of blood—by the British soldiers the other day, were yesterday connected with eleven murders, attempted murders and other violent crimes. These include attacks on members of the Shanghai Municipal Police apparently perpetrated for no other reason than to intimidate.

There was the grand assault on the so-called Asia Club, a notorious gambling den at 65 Gordon Road, on the evening of November 9, 1938. A party was being given at the "Club" at the time, to celebrate the engagement of a Korean and a Chinese girl, when a group of Chinese appeared about the building, threw hand-grenades and fired volleys of shots. They used pistols belonging to the evil group of weapons.

Again, one of the pistols was used in an attempted robbery in Lane 506, Taku Road, a Chinese dry-cleaning shop last June. This crime was committed at night, and when the shop owner's son raised an alarm one of the bandits fired a shot.

Attack on Sikh Police

More startling was an attempt to murder two Sikh constables of the S.M.P. while they were on patrol on Jessfield Road on the forenoon of June 15, 1939. Several armed gangsters fired some twenty shots at the two policemen, who pursued them. The bandits escaped, and the Indians fortunately were not hit, though they had close calls.

Pistols in the murderous collection again were used to intimidate the staff of the University Press, 130 Ningpo Road, on the evening of June 17, 1939. A number of shots were fired, and a hand-grenade of the "potato-masher" type was placed outside the front door. The hand-grenade did not explode and was removed and rendered harmless.

The scene now shifts back to the "badlands." On June 20 some bandits tried to rob 436 and 438 Robison Road under cover of darkness. The occupants of the houses gave an alarm and the bad men fired four shots as they retreated without plunder.

At the end of July an S.M.P. search-party ran into an armed gang at Stone Bridge and Sinza Roads in broad daylight. There was an immediate exchange of fire and two members of the band were shot dead while a third was wounded.

When gangsters entered a cotton mill in Lane 255, Singapore Road, they were successful in robbing the office. Before they left, however, one of their number fired a shot, probably to show how fierce they were.

The same gang had been at the mill two days previously, when they had demanded $500 saying they would "call again." To show that they really meant business, they had fired one shot.

The dark record of the group of pistols includes the murder of one Chang Yue-tsung in August, 1939, while he was walking in South Zau Ka Zah village, in the turbulent west.

Chinese Constable Killed

The sensational attack on an S.M.P. traffic post in the outside-roads area on October 20 involved the same set of death-dealing firearms. A group of Chinese opened fire on the post at the intersection of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads, killed Chinese Constable No. 3378 and tried to murder the Sikh policeman who was also on traffic duty at the crossing. No motive was apparent in this case except a determination to intimidate the Settlement Police who were doing their duty in the area.

Another murderous assault on Settlement policemen involved two Sikhs, a naik and a constable, who were fired upon outside 1464 Jessfield Road. They escaped with their lives.

Finally, the fatal aggregation of automatics figured in a mysterious and protracted shooting in badlands territory in the vicinity of Edinburgh and Brenan Roads during the early hours of October 19, last. The reason for this affray could not be ascertained by the Police, and it was not learned if there were any casualties.

MAR 2 1940

“Tug” Wilson
Murder Pistol
Is Identified

The 13 armed men allegedly attached to a Wang Ching-wei faction who were arrested by a British military patrol off Crescent Avenue last Tuesday carried three pistols used in the attack on the China Evening News, 160 Avenue Edward VII. by terrorists on July 22, 1939.

This attack, it will be recalled, resulted in the death of Mr. Albert “Tug” Wilson, American part-owner of the New Ritz Bar, who was killed by terrorists when he courageously attempted to stop them.

Nine pistols were seized by the British military when they detained the 13 men last Tuesday. Of these, two Mausers and an Astra pistol were used in the attack on the China Evening News. Mr. Wilson was killed when he rushed toward the escaping terrorists from his bar across the street, at the corner of Avenue Edward VII and “Blood Alley.”

Linked To Other Crimes

This revelation, which also connected other pistols seized on the gangsters with several other armed crimes, was made known yesterday as a result of investigations by S.M.P. ballistic experts.

It will be recalled that, immediately after the British military last Tuesday arrested the men, a detachment from the Japanese Gendarmerie rushed to the scene and demanded custody of the weapons—although they were not at all concerned over obtaining custody of the men themselves.

The S.M.C. Arms Identification Bureau also revealed yesterday that the 10 pistols seized belonged to a group of 20 weapons, exclusive of the nine seized on Tuesday. Six of these 20 have already been seized by the police.

The crimes in which these six pistols, belonging to the same group with the nine pistols seized Tuesday, were used numbered no less than 11, including armed robberies, intimidations, gunfights with the police, murders and attempted murders.

Used At Asia Club

At 8 p.m. on September 11, 1938, some of these weapons, and a number of hand-grenades were used in a shooting affray in the premises of the Asia Club, a gambling den at 65 Gordon Road, it was stated. At the time of the throwing of these grenades, a party was in progress to celebrate the engagement of a Korean and a Chinese woman.

Some of these weapons were also used in a battle between members of an S.M.P. search party and an armed gang on Stone Bridge and Sinza Road, at 7:40 a.m. on July 21, 1939. Two members of the gang were shot dead and another was injured on that occasion.

While on duty at the corner of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads, at 6:45 p.m. on October 10, 1939, Chinese Police Constable 3378 was murdered by men armed with some of these pistols, while Sikh Police Constable 459 escaped death narrowly.

There did not appear to be any motive for this offense other than the intimidation of members of the Municipal Police, it was stated.

Traced To Murder

At 6:30 p.m. on October 8, 1939, one Chang Yue-tsung was shot dead while walking in South Kau Ka Zah Village, outside S.M.P. limits, by men who fired from weapons included in the group, it was revealed.

At 9 p.m. on June 20, 1939, these weapons were used in an armed robbery at 436 and 438 Robison Road, outside Municipal Police limits. Four shots were fired by the men when escaping from the premises. Men armed with some of these pistols intimidated employees of the University Press, 130 Ningpo Road, at 8:50 p.m., on June 17, 1939. A number of shots were fired and a hand-grenade of the potato-masher type was found unexploded outside the front entrance of the premises.

An armed robbery in a cotton mill in 255, House 101 Singapore Road, outside Municipal Police limits, was carried out at 5 p.m. on June 18, 1939, with the aid of these guns, it was further stated. One shot was fire before the robbers left the premises.

The same robbers had previously entered the mill on June 16, 1939, demanding $500, stating that they would call again, and firing one shot to emphasize their demands.

Shot At Sikh Officers

Men armed with some of these guns attempted to kill two Sikh Police Constables at 11:20 a.m. on June 15, 1939, while the latter were patrolling Jessfield Road. The policemen, neither of whom were injured, gave chase, but the armed men made good their escape behind a fusillade of 20 shots.

An attempted armed robbery took place in a dry cleaning shop at 506, House 69 Taku Road, at 10:20 p.m. on May 23, 1939, by men carrying weapons belonging to the same group. One shot was fired by one of the gangsters when an alarm was raised by a young boy.

A number of shots were fired outside Police limits, in the vicinity of Edinburgh and Brenan Roads at 5:55 a.m. on October 19, 1939, the weapons again belonging to the same category. Enquiries failed to reveal any information on the reason for this shooting, it was stated.

Finally, an attempted murder of Naik 182 and Sikh Police Constable 594 was carried out with the aid of these weapons outside 1464 Jessfield Road on June 27, 1939, tests carried out by the Arms Identification Bureau revealed.

Hwa Pao, National Herald, Shun Pao :-

CONDITIONS IN THE "BADLANDS"

Lawlessness prevails in the outside roads
area in the Western District due to the presence of
undesirable elements. At certain places, owing to
interference by policemen of the Shanghai City Government,
officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police are finding it
extremely difficult to carry out their duties.
Yesterday afternoon a reporter of the Dah
Chung News Agency (大中社 ) toured the "Badlands" area
and the following is a record of what he saw :-
On every electric pole in Zau Ka Tu (commonly
known as Brenan Piece), Jessfield Road, Robison Road,
Brenan Road and vicinity are to be found coloured paper
slips bearing absurd slogans.
Puppet policemen were on duty along Yu Yuen
Road. At the intersection of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads,
a pedestrian was knocked down by a ricsha. A dispute arose
and when a Municipal constable attempted to mediate, a
number of puppet policemen went up and did everything
possible to obstruct the efforts of the Municipal officer,
with the result that neither side could deal with the
dispute. Eventually the ricsha coolie and the pedestrian,
fearing trouble, moved away.

Ying flower pot shop (科大影盆景店), House 83C Yu Yuen

Eight puppet policemen were posted on duty at
the intersection of Columbia Road and Amherst Avenue; their
attitude was hostile. At about this time it happened
that a thief stole a woollen garment from a house nearby
and was caught by Municipal officers. As the officers

CHINA PRESS

NOV 12, 1939

Police Identify
Bullet Which
Killed Puppet

Gun Used Also Figured
In Wedding Massacre
On October 21

Ballistic experts of the Shanghai
Municipal Police have identified
one of the bullets with which a
"Ta Tao" official was assassinated
last week, as coming from the
same gun used in the mass murder
of a "Ta Tao" wedding party on
October 21.

The bullet from a Mauser pistol
was one of several which cut down
Loo Tse-ping, Chief of the Japan-
ese Special Service Section "Self-
protection Corps" and his assistant,
Yang Ching-hai, as the two were
entertaining about 40 guests at a
large dinner party in the Van Lee
Restaurant, Chekiang and Foochow
Roads on November 9. The assassins
made a clean get-away.

The previous assassination was
staged on the afternoon of Octo-
ber 22 at the wedding ceremony of
Tu Cheng-shan "Director of
Publicity" of the Japanese spon-
sored Ta Min Hui.

The latter function attended by
150 guests was in full swing at
the Medium Club, Weihaiwei Road
when, suddenly, indiscriminate

tempt which left the puppet official

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

NOV 1 1 1939

Pistols Connected
With Other Crimes
Police Push Investigation
Of Double Murder ; Many
Suspects Remanded

While the Settlement Police yes-
terday renewed their search for the
actual murderers and the pistols
used in the slaying of two "bad
lands" officials in a Foochow Road
restaurant on Thursday evening, it
was discovered, from examination of
the cartridge cases found at the
scene, that the weapons had figured
in several recent terroristic shot-
ings here. The murdered men were
connected with a "special service
corps" sponsored by the Wang Chung-
wei group in the West.
Three high-powered Mauser pistols
and a 32-calibre automatic were used
by the assassins on Thursday at the
Van Lee Restaurant, Foochow and
Hoopeh Roads, some dozen cartridge
cases from these weapons being
found. The ballistics section of the
S.M.P. has now ascertained that these
pistols were used also in the whole-
sale shooting at a wedding party in
Weihaiwei Road on October 22, in a
political assassination in the street
at Yunnan and Foochow Roads, and
in a dinner party shooting in Bing
Von Ka, off Canton Road. In the
Bing Vong Ka case, which took
place on October 14, a singsong girl
was killed and a Japanese guest was
slightly wounded.
Seventeen suspects were arrested
by Louza Station detectives at the
restaurant on Thursday night and
were brought before the First Spe-
cial District Court yesterday morn-
ing. At the request of the police,
they were remanded in custody for
a week pending further investiga-
tions. Some of the men involved
have previous criminal records in
the terroristic and armed robbery
fields.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
NOV 10 1939
“Bad Lands” Men
Slain at Banquet
Wang Ching-wei Official
And Interpreter Riddled
In Louza Restaurant

Two Chinese said to have been in
the employ of the Wang Ching-wei
organization in the western “bad
lands” and the Japanese military, re-
spectively, were riddled with bullets
last night at a dinner given by one
of them in a restaurant at 514 Foo-
chow Road, corner of Hoopeh Road,
in the heart of the Louza amusement
district. The assassins, who used
high-powered Mauser pistols and
smaller automatics, escaped. Although
a number of the guests and members
of the restaurant staff were question-
ed it could not be ascertained at an
early hour this morning whether the
murders were committed by persons
present at the dinner or by outsiders.
A fusillade of shots almost instantly
killed the two men at whom the
shooting was directed, and no-one
else apparently was wounded.
The host at the party was named
Yang Ching-hai and he was giving
the dinner in celebration of his having
recently been appointed to a post in
the Wang Ching-wei organization in
the western area. He had invited
about forty Chinese to the feast, and
his guests were seated at several
tables when the shooting started.
The time was 7.15 and the party was
getting well under way.

Terrified Guests Flee

In the confusion that followed,
tables and chairs were upset, and
yellow wine spilt from pewter pots
mingled with the blood of the vic-
tims. The terrified guests made for
other rooms or for the stairway and
by the time the police arrived more
than half had fled. The remainder
were closely questioned by detectives
but up to a late hour had not given
a comprehensible account of how the
shooting began. The police found
about a dozen empty cartridge cases
on the floor of the banqueting hall.
These cases, which differed in calibre,
were being examined by Headquart-
ers ballistics experts last night and
early this morning.
The second man killed by the as-
sassins was one Lu Tzu-ping, a Ja-
panese-speaking Chinese, who was
also employed in the western area.
Like Yang, he was shot several times,
the bullets piercing vital parts and
causing instantaneous death. He was
said to have been working in the
outside roads district as an interpreter
between the Japanese military and
Chinese working for the “reformed”
administration.
Both men were rushed to the Lester
Hospital in a Fire Brigade ambulance
after the shooting had been reported.
They were pronounced dead im-
mediately upon arrival.

Many Suspects Questioned

It is understood that seventeen or
eighteen persons were taken to Louza
Police Station last night and inter-
rogated about the crime. Although
no definite conclusion could be drawn
from the preliminary questioning, it
was held as quite probable that the
shooting was the result of internal
trouble among the “bad lands” gentry.
Analogous cases, in which rivalry
between factions within the “refor-
med” group has led to bloodshed, are
well known to the police.
Early this morning clues were being
“worked” by the detectives on the
case, asking definitely to establish
the motive and identity of the gang
responsible.

SHANGHAI TIMES.

NOV 10 1939

Two Chinese
Assassinated
In Restaurant

Shot In Course Of Big
Banquet By Guests
Or Intruders

VICTIMS CONNECTED
WITH JAPANESE

Two Chinese, allegedly connected with Japanese sponsored administrations in the western Outside Roads area, were shot and killed by three gunmen in the course of a banquet given by one of them at the Van Lee Restaurant at 514, Foochow Road, near Hoopeh Road, yesterday evening.

The latest brutal assassination to be staged in a restaurant, took place at about 7.15 p.m. just as the party was completing its dinner, which was given by one of the victims, Yang Chin-hai, 41, in honour of the second victim, Lo Chih-ping, 30.

As far as could be ascertained last night, Yang was allegedly a secret service corps chief attached to an organization in Jessfield, while Lo was attached as a translator to the Japanese Gendarmerie in the Western district. Chinese sources claimed last night that Yang had been appointed chief of the Japanese sponsored gendarmerie corps and that he had picked Lo to be his assistant and was honouring him at the banquet when they were both shot.

Despite the fact that detectives of Louza Police Station, upon rushing to the scene of the killing, managed to detain 12 guests and three waiters for interrogation, up to a late hour last night it had not been definitely cleared up whether the two victims were killed by guests or by assassins, who had managed to walk into the banquet room.

Three Gunmen

One thing was cleared up, and that is the fact that there were three gunmen who did the firing, killing both Yang and Lo instantly. Lo sustained four bullet wounds in the abdomen, while Yang died as the result of three bullet wounds in the head. Ten shots are believed to have been fired in all, and empty cartridge cases picked up by the police showed that Mauser and .32 calibre pistols were used. The empty cartridge cases were last night handed over to the ballistic expert of the S.M.P. for examination.

There were about 40 to 50 guests
at the banquet on the second floor
of the Van Lee Restaurant, includ-
ing three women, when the shoot-
ing occurred. The guests arrived
at about 6 p.m., partook of drinks
and then sat down to dinner. Just
as they were nearing the final
course, being seated at five large
tables, the shooting took place and,
within a few seconds, the whole
restaurant was thrown into the
uproar as guests and waiters fled,
the gunmen making good their
escape in the excitement
Conflicting Stories
Little information could be
obtained by the police from the 12
guests and three waiters, whom
they had detained for interrogation.
Those who did speak gave conflict-
ing stories. Some maintained that
the shooting was done by three of
the guests, others claimed that the
gunmen had walked into the room
a few minutes before they open-
ed fire.
All those interrogated yesterday
professed that they had not the
slightest knowledge of what could
be the motive behind the assassina-
tions. They discounted the theory
that the killings might have been
carried out on political grounds,
but rather favoured the idea that
the murders were due to some per-
sonal feud.
The waiters, on being question-
ed, stated that they did not see
the gunmen and did not know
what actually occurred, as they
were outside the room when the
shooting took place.
Most of these detained for ques-
tioning reside in the western dis-
trict, near Jessfield. They stated that
they were old friends of Yang and
that they had no grudge against
him. The host and most of the
guests were natives of Yangchow,
it was ascertained, the remainder
being natives of Chinkiang.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

NOV 10 1932

17 Face
Charges

Guests At Restaurant
Seized By Police
After Killing

The shoot up at the Van
Li Restaurant at 514 Foo-
chow Road last night that
spelled the demise of two
glorified barbers, who had a
big say in the activities of
the "Self-Defense Corps" in
the badlands, echoed raucous-
ly in the First Special District
Court this morning when a
noisy crowd of 17 blabbering
disreputable men stood in the pri-
soners' dock on a writ of deten-
tion as suspects in connection with
the murders.

Among the suspects is a mem-
ber of the "corps," it was learned.
Pending further inquiries into the
assassination case, the men will
be held under detention at Louza
station to ascertain whether any
of them had a hand in the killing
of the host at last night's dinner
party, Yang Chine-hai, chief of
the "corps" who stooped 10 well-
aimed bullets to die instantly at
the hands of the assassins, and
of Lo Che-pin, a guest, who was
shot seven times to meet the same
fate.

All Guests

All the suspects were guests at
the party. They were rounded up
by a raiding party from Louza
station composed of Detective-In-
spector W. Hutton, Chinese Detec-
tive-Sergeants 342 and 93, and
others, who rushed to the scene of
the murders when the first alarm
was given. Twelve spent cartridges
and five rounds of ammunition
were found on the premises. In
view of the fact that the killing
may have been perpetrated by
rival members of the "Self Defense
Corps," the investigators rounded
up 17 of the guests, it was stated.

It was ascertained by the
Shanghai Evening Post today that
both the victims had been barbers
in Yokohama before they came to
Shanghai. Yang had been hold-
ing forth in the badlands as the
chief of the "corps," while Lo had
been allegedly connected with the
Ta Tao Special Service Section
headquarters off Jessfield Road in
the capacity of an interpreter.

Calm Attack

The shoot-up took place around
7.30 p.m. as some 45 guests were
about to begin the first course of
the dinner on five separate tables
in Rooms 22-23. Five or six long-
gowned men suddenly appeared
at the doors to the rooms and
three of them calmly made way

to the tables with drawn guns.
Before anybody could move, they
opened fire at the host and Lo in
rapid succession. When the din
was over, the gunmen had gone.
Upon this scene of confusion came
the raiding party a few minutes
later to round up the suspects
Today's court proceedings were
in the hands of Mr. Paul Y. Ru,
municipal advocate. It is under-
stood that those who can furnish
proof of their innocence during
their detention will be released
by the police.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
NOV 4 - 1939
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D.
Date

Wang Ching-wei
Man in Hold-up
Police Watchman Shot
As Three Robbers Escape
With $10,400

One of two gangsters arrested shortly after they, together with three accomplices, had perpetrated an armed robbery in the premises of a Chinese oil hong at 243 Canton Road at 6.50 p.m. yesterday when $10,400 in bank-notes were stolen, is said to have admitted that he is connected with the Wang Ching-wei movement and at the time of his arrest was in possession of a Mauser pistol and 26 rounds of ammunition of the type used in the attack on the premises of a newspaper at 160 Avenue Edward VII, on July 22. Chinese police watchman No. 552 who courageously attempted to prevent the gangsters from leaving the alleyway through which they managed to escape, was seriously wounded in the left arm, the bullet ricochetting and finally lodging in his chest from where it was extracted in the Lester Chinese Hospital.

When the officer on duty at Central Station heard the first account of the affair from the injured watchman who, notwithstanding his wounds, had walked to the station to make his report, he little realized that of the five men and a woman connected with the daring robbery, two men and the woman had already fallen into the hands of a Reserve Unit search-party operating at the corner of Fokien Road and Avenue Edward VII.

Police Attend

An alarm was immediately raised and a police party rushed to the scene. Upon questioning the victims of the hold-up, detectives in charge of the case learned that five men, four of them armed, had entered the premises the ground-floor of which is used as a godown while on the first floor the offices of the hong are located, and, while two of the armed men remained downstairs, the other three proceeded upstairs.

Completely taken by surprise, the employees of the hong had no other alternative but to obey orders and they were herded into an adjoining room where two of the though began to search them while the other forced two of the employees to open a safe from which they took $2,400 in bank-notes.

Meanwhile, the search of the terrified employees of the hong yielded $8,000 in cash which one of them had just brought there.

After threatening their victims in the usual manner, the men decamped through the same alleyway which leads on to Honan Road. As soon as the thugs had left the building, however, the robbed employees began to blow their police whistles, thereby rousing the watchman who until then had been sitting in his hut. He attempted to prevent the escape of the gangsters and was thereupon shot with a .38 calibre bullet at point-blank range.

Coolie Gives Chase
Meanwhile, a coolie employed in
a native bank with premises in the
same alleyway, who was proceeding
towards the street to call a rickshaw,
saw what had happened and, not-
withstanding the danger he was fac-
ing, gave chase to two members of
the armed quintet, and to the woman
who ran with them as they proceeded
south on Honan Road towards Avenue
Edward VII.
When the thugs arrived on that
thoroughfare, they ran in a westerly
direction. Undaunted, the coolie con-
tinued in his pursuit and drew the
attention of a French C.P.C. on duty
outside Poste Mallet, to what was
happening. The latter thereupon also
gave chase and the two bandits, as
well as the woman, fell into the arms
of a Reserve Unit search-party stand-
ing at the corner of Fokien Road and
Avenue Edward VII.
The three arrested persons were
taken to Louza police station and it
was there discovered that, the other
three who had escaped in a different
direction—the group having broken
up at the mouth of the alleyway—
actually carried the money and had
made good their escape.
The arrested persons were sent to
Central Station where investigations
are being continued. Up to an early
hour this morning, ballistic experts
were busy examining the seized
Mauser pistol but the result of these
examinations was not divulged.
As one of the arrested men, who
gave his name as Sze Tsengwo,
had admitted that he was a
member of a pro-Wang Ching-wei
terrorist group, however, it was be-
lieved possible that some connection
may be established between the men
arrested yesterday and those respon-
sible for the shooting affray on
Avenue Edward VII in July. Sze
is reported to have told detectives
that prior to the Sino-Japanese hostil-
ities, he was a member of the Peace
Maintenance Corps. He is also said
to have two gunwound scars on his
chest and neck respectively and it was
believed likely that he has been con-
nected with previous shoot-ups.
While it has not been established in
what way the arrested woman—a
mere girl—is connected with the
gang, it was presumed that she car-
ried the pistols to the scene of the
robbery.

Ta Ying Yeh Pao of October 28 :- 29.10.39 (174)
THE SPECIAL SERVICE CORPS
Recently a so-called Special Service Corps
was established in the Western District of Shanghai, of a
similar nature to that of the Huang Dao Association (黄道会).
It specializes in assassinations and abductions. The members
of the corps are all loafers. As Wu Yuin-fu (吴云甫),
head of the corps, and his followers including one Chang
Wei-yung (张回永) have committed many cases of abduction
and extortion, the Japanese authorities the day before
yesterday issued a notification announcing that an
investigation will be made into the activities of the corps.

Chinese-American Daily News and Ta Mei Wan Pao (3/9) :- 4 9. 19 (FN)

PRIMARY SCHOOL IN WESTERN DISTRICT OCCUPIED

The Kang Kung Primary School ( 幹工小学 ),
No. 1500 Brenan Road in the Western District, was established
20 years ago by Tan Kang-chen ( 陳幹臣 ). At present,
Wu Chung-yuen ( 吳宗源 ) is the principal of the school
and has about 1,000 pupils.
On the early morning of September 3, 5 or 6
well dressed male Chinese visited the school and told
Principal Wu that the school must be closed immediately.
The visitors threatened Wu and claimed that they belonged
to a certain body.
Knowing that it is difficult to deal with
these visitors, Wu told the latter that he could not
find suitable houses for the pupils and asked if a section
of the school premises could still be used to house the
pupils. Arrangements were then made that the visitors
would occupy three rooms of the school and that huts
would be erected on the recreation ground.
At noon yesterday, a large number of persons
entered the school and commenced functioning.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.
20859

5 1939

Jessfield Rd. School
House Locked

Italians Discontinue
Searches of Premises

Italian marine have discontinued
periodically inspecting the premises
at 1081 Jessfield Road since 2 p.m.
yesterday after the gates leading to
the house were locked and a notice
in Chinese and signed by the
Japanese Gendarmerie was affixed,

mises.

Shortly after noon on Friday, it
was officially learned, an Italian
patrol entered the premises and
after a routine search found that a
Chinese was hovering in a corner.
He was taken to the Robison Road
headquarters of the Italians from
where he was released after having
been questioned, it having been
established that he was not con-
nected with other terrorists or
"Ta Tao" police.

Reports circulated yesterday to the
effect that truck-loads of women
and bedding had been unloaded and
taken into the premises on Thursday
afternoon, were emphatically denied
in official quarters, where it was
emphasized that regular inspections
had been made of the premises until

Since the door has been locked,

reinforcements taking up positions

22834
AUG 5 1935

1081 Jessfield Road
Guarded by Italians
Thursday's Incident
Considered Closed

The premises of the Tsaoji Primary
School at 1081, Jessfield Road, where,
it will be recalled, some 26 alleged
pro-Wang Ching-wei terrorists were

by an Italian marine patrol on Thurs-

Rumours to the effect that ten of
