CHINA PRESS.
Gunmen Still AUG 5 1939
Being Held By
Italian Forces
26820
Armed Mob Arrested
In Jessfield Not
Handed Over
CASE BECOMES
POLITICAL AFFAIR
Matter Said Now In
Hands Of Italian
Embassy

Eighteen Chinese gunmen, arrest-
ed by the Italian Marines in
Jessfield on Thursday morning, were
still in the hands of the Italian
Shore Naval Headquarters, 62
Robison Road last night.
This information was obtained by
THE CHINA PRESS from the highest
official authority about 10 p.m.
It contradicts Thursday reports
that the gunmen had been handed
over to the Japanese gendarmerie
after it was discovered that they
were connected with the local "Ta
Tao Government."
Latest reports on the case are to
the effect that, although the Japan-
ese have made representations to
the Italian authorities for the re-
lease of the men, these overtures
have not yet been complied with.

Embassy Notified

Although well-informed circles
last night considered it likely that
the men will be released or handed
over to the Japanese, the local
Italian naval authorities are not
taking the responsibility for such
action on their own shoulders.

The case, it was also reported last
night has been turned over to the
Italian Embassy and has thereby
ceased to be a military matter but
a political affair. It also was re-
garded as probable last night that
Rome may even be consulted before
the gunmen and their weapons are
handed over to the Japanese.
The 18 gunmen, described as
having some connection with the
local "Ta Tao" regime as members
of the "Special Service Corps of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern League," a pro-Wang
Ching-wei group, were arrested by
Italian Marines on the premises of
the Zao Ka Do Merchants' Street
Union, 1081 Jessfield Road, about 9
a.m. Thursday.

Representations Made

An Italian patrol spotted a Chin-
ese plainclothesman walking along
Jessfield Road and ordered the man
stop. Instead of obeying the order,
the fellow dashed into the Mer-
chants' Street Union building. The
Italians followed and to their sur-
prise, encountered 17 more gunmen.
Under orders to pick up all
Chinese gunmen found in their
sector, the Italians ordered the lot
to surrender and hand over their
arms. The gunmen offered no re-
sistance and the men were accord-
ingly taken to Italian Headquarters
on Robison Road.

Representations for the release of
the men were made by the Japanese
gendarmerie and the "Ta Tao"
regime, whereupon the Italian naval
authorities referred the matter to
the Italian Embassy.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
21835

AUG 5 1939

Mistaken Terrorists

The Italian Marine authorities are to be con-
gratulated on their action in Jessfield Road on
Thursday when they rounded up a party of
armed men and detained them. It was dis-
covered later that the 16 men were members
of the Ta Tao Government staff and thereupon
they were released, but the circumstances gov-
erning the case warranted the action of the
Italian Marines. An armed man was seen en-
tering, apparently from a Municipal road, the
premises of a former Chinese school, and the
Italian patrol summoned reinforcements in
order to detain him and others found on the
premises. They wore no uniform which would
provide evidence of official identification, and
as they were carrying Mauser pistols and hand
grenades the Italian Marines were only carry-
ing out their duty in detaining the men, especial-
ly as their particular official function in this
part of Shanghai's "badlands" could not be im-
mediately ascertained. Some pertinent inquiry
arises from the incident. Shanghai, at present,
is almost on a war-time footing as far as internal
defence measures are concerned, and armed
police parties are patrolling the streets in order
to counteract threats of gangster activities, the
source of which continues to present a baffling
puzzle to the foreign authorities. Conditions are
so serious as to necessitate the display of
armed force because of the gangster menace,
politically inspired, but why Ta Tao men wear-
ing dungarees and other forms of nondescript
clothing should be found carrying Mauser
pistols and hand grenades is a situation worthy
of deeper examination. All the hand grenades
flung at newspaper offices and other institutions
are supposed to have been the weapons of the
lawless elements against whom the foreign au-
thorities, co-operating with the Japanese and
the Chinese administration under their con-
trol, are operating in the interest of peace and
order. If legitimately-employed Ta Tao
police, guards, employees or whatever they
might be called, are roaming around with hand
grenades tied to their belts they ought to be
warned of the consequences. The police can-
not be blamed if accidents happen.

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
AUG 4 1939
Italians Free
16 Arrested
Suspects
Ta Tao Men Mistaken
For Terrorists by
Marines
Sixteen armed men, some clad in
dungarees and some in foreign
clothes, but none in any uniform
whatsoever, who were rounded up by
Italian marines shortly after 9 yester-
day morning at the Tsaoji Primary
School, 1081 Jessfield Road, were re-
leased by the Italian authorities
about 4 p.m. yesterday when it was
learned that the men were members
of the Ta Tao Government. The
men, who were visibly armed, were
placed under arrest by orders of the
Italian Commander in the Western
Sector after they had been spotted
by a patrol of marines yesterday
morning. The commander could not
understand to which particular or-
ganization the men belonged, so he
ordered them taken to Italian marine
headquarters at 62 Robison Road for
questioning.
The men were originally arrested
on suspicion of being connected with
terroristic organizations, but when
their true status was disclosed to the
Italian authorities they were released
and their weapons, which included
Mausers and hand-grenades, and
which were seized by the marines
during the round-up, were restored
to them.
Marines Surround Building
When the patrol saw an armed
man enter the premises of the Tsaoji
Primary School, they informed
their headquarters by telephone with
the result that a few minutes later,
a truckload of 50 additional marines
arrived on the scene and surrounded
the building which is actually situated
in "Ta Tao" territory. They entered
and placed 16 armed men under arrest
whilst a large quantity of Mauser
pistols, potato-masher type hand-
grenades and other weapons were
seized and taken to the Italian head-
quarters, with the suspects.
It was first believed that the
arrested men were members of the
terrorist group which was respon-
sible for the shooting affrays on
Avenue Edward VII and Hankow
Roads on the evening of July 29
when an American and three Chinese
were killed and 20 persons injured.
The gang, as will be recalled, had
a fortified hide-out in a building
situated inside Lane 95, Edinburgh
Road until a few days ago when the
Japanese gendarmerie was stated to
have informed the head of the gang,
who lives at No. 76 Jessfield Road,
that the building in question would
have to be vacated, the arms sur-
rendered and the men accommodated
at No. 76 Jessfield Road.
It was therefore presumed that the
gang, not wishing to live in their
newly assigned quarters, thought that
the premises of the Tsaoji Primary
School could be altered to serve as a
new hide-out and they accordingly
went to the school yesterday morn-
ing, informing the principal that the
building would have to be vacated
within nine days.

Whilst 23 men were already inside
the building when the Italian patrol
came to the scene, the last of the
men was about to enter at that
precise moment. Arguing that the
armed man had been walking on a
Settlement Road, the Italian patrol
immediately informed headquarters
in view of the fact that for the past
few months, they have had strict in-
structions to disarm anyone found
carrying a weapon without a proper
licence within their sector.
At the time, it could not be known
that so many men were inside the
building and with sufficient re-
inforcements on the scene to be able
to cope with any eventuality, several
officers and men entered the premises
and made a careful search with the
result that 16 were arrested and a
large number of pistols and hand
grenades seized.
It was thought that the men
in question could not possibly
have any right to carry arms even
in "Ta Tao" territory because no
representations had been made to
the Italians by the Japanese-sponsored
administration. While the Italians
were searching the premises, a
number of uniformed "Ta Tao"
policemen idly stood by after having
respectfully bowed to the armed men
when they entered the school
building a few minutes previously.
The Italian marines meant business
and this was probably known inside
the school building so that no resist-
ance was offered to the Italian
search. Machine-guns were placed at
various strategic points in the vicinity
of the building whilst all the marines
stood by with cocked rifles and fixed
bayonets ready to go into action at
any moment.

CHINA PRESS
AUG 4 1939
Fast Action Taken
In Western Areas
WhenRumorsSpread
Fresh Plot To Attack
“Fleet Street” Is
Alleged
ITALIAN MARINES
HAND OVER MOB
16 Terrorists Placed
In Custody Of
Japanese
Acting on rumors that a
number of gunmen from the
“badlands” had crossed into
the Settlement and were bent
on carrying out another
shooting affray in Shanghai’s
“Fleet Street,” S.M.P. reser-
ves turned out about 5 p.m.
yesterday and staged a
lightning search of cars,
trams and buses along Bub-
bling Well Road.
The police, at the same time, set
up barricades along extra-Settle-
ment roads of the Western District
in an effort to prevent other gun-
men from entering the Settlement.
Many of the barricades were still
in place at a late hour last night
and there was indication that they
may be kept in place until after
August 13, the second anniversary
of the outbreak of Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai area.
Traffic Held Up
As a result of the swift police
action, traffic was held up along
Lubbing Well Road. Search parties
made an effort to stop and examine
every car coming from the Western
District. And so strict was police
vigilance that few cars escaped this
search.
French Police authorities, co-
operating with the Settlement,
started intensive search of pedes-
trians and cars along Avenue
Edward VII, the city’s “Newspaper
Row,” about 5 p.m. This work was
carried on until after 10 p.m.
Rumors of one type or another
flew thick and fast in the news-
paper district. One report was
to the effect that nine car loads
of terrorists from the ‘badlands’
were on their way into the city
to “shoot up” the newspapers.
Whether there was anything to
this report may never be known.
If this were true, then it is to
be presumed that the mobsters
were frightened off by sudden
police precautions. The Police
admitted that a few gunmen
were supposed to be inside the
Settlement, hence the searches.
Some of these gunmen are said
to have been members of the
gang involved in the affair on
Jessfield Road yesterday morn-
ing.

Gang Grabbed

Sixteen members of the
Special Service Corps of the "Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
League," a pro-Wang Ching-wei
group, armed with Mauser pistols,
hand-grenades and swords were
surrounded and taken into custody
by Italian Marines yesterday morning.

The terrorists were rounded up
by the Italian force after they had
forcibly occupied the Zao Ka Doo
Merchants' Street Union at 1081
Jessfield Road—which is within the
International Settlement perimeter
but actually outside the Settlement
limits.

Barricading themselves within
the building shortly after 9 a.m.,
the terrorists appeared to be ready
to resist the Italian Marines after
these were rushed to the scene in
a military truck. However, when it
was demanded of them to surrender,
they meekly gave themselves up.

Disarmed, the terrorists were
herded into a military truck and
taken to the Italian headquarters at
2 Robison Road.

Handed Over

The 16 arrested men were
handed over by the Italian
naval authorities to the Japanese gendarmerie yesterday afternoon. This action was taken,
according to the Italian Naval
Headquarters, because the terrorists were nabbed inside
Japanese occupied territory.
The Italian officials claimed
that they had no other alternative.

Sixteen pistols seized by the
Italians when the arrests were
made are also reported to have
been handed over to the Japanese although the Shanghai
Municipal Police made application for the custody of the guns.
It is understood that the police
wanted to examine the guns for
possible murder and armed robber weapons.

Wore Foreign Clothes

According to reports available
yesterday evening, the armed gang
set out from their headquarters at
8.45 a.m. yesterday. Contrary to
previous reports, it was stated
yesterday afternoon that there were
not more than 22 in the gang. The
terrorists were dressed in foreign
clothes, some of them wearing overalls. All freely and even unnecessarily displayed their weapons.

Eye-witnesses report that "Ta
Tao" policemen bowed respectfully
to the gangsters as they passed by.

With the arrival of the Italian
force shortly after the occupation of
the building by the terrorists, the
street was cleared and shops in the
immediate vicinity closed their
doors. Normalcy was restored
shortly after 11 a.m.

Italian Marines Disarm, Arrest
Terrorists

Big Gang
Of 50 Held
In Badlands

Pro-Wang Mob Foiled
Trying To Break
Into School

EXCITEMENT RUNS
HIGH IN BRENAN

Gangsters Defy Order,
Finally Surrender
To Marines

Tension gripped Brenan
Piece area this morning
when armed terrorists, de-
clared to be members of
the pro-Wang Ching wei
"special service corps,"
almost clashed with Italian
marines outside a house at
1081 Jessfield Road.
Barricading themselves be-
hind the protective walls of
the house, formerly the head-
quarters of the Chinese
Volunteers' Corps and now
occupied by the Tsaoyi Primary
School, the terrorists, numbering
between 40 and 50 according to
an unofficial report, defied the
Italian defense forces but finally
surrendered. They were disarmed
and herded into an Italian mili-
tary truck, No. 218, and taken to
Italian headquarters. Official
sources declare that 26 were placed
into custody and military Mausers
and a big assortment of weapons
seized. An eyewitness account
states that a big quantity of hand
grenades was loaded on a ricksha
and taken to the Italian head-
quarters under escort.

Moved Headquarters
The armed terrorists made their
appearance outside the building
shortly after 9 o'clock this morn-
ing. It is reported that they were
sent from their headquarters at 76
Jessfield Road, formerly the re-
sidence of General Chen Tiao
yuan, member of the Military
Advisory Council of the National
Government. These terrorists had
only recently moved their head-
quarters to 76 Jessfield Road from
a house at Edinburgh Road, it is
said.

Between 40 and 50 of the
terrorists, believed to be of the
same gang responsible for the at-
tack on the offices of the Chinese
American Daily News and the
Chinese Evening News recently
appeared in front of 1081 Jess-
field Road this morning. Some
were in overalls and others in for-
eign dresses. They were all armed
with big swords, military Mausers
and hand-grenades. A delegation
of them went into the school and
ordered the evacuation of the
building within nine days, an-
nouncing that they intended to
convert that building into another
headquarters.

Receive Bows

The terrorists commanded great
respect from the "Ta Tao" police,
according to eye-witness accounts.
All of the constables bowed to
them when passing past.

Italian military authorities re-
ceived information of their presence
a few minutes later and a party
of marines, declared in one source
200 strong and estimated to num-
ber 50 by official sources, was
rushed to the scene. They sur-
rounded the premises and demand-
ed the terrorists to surrender. The
latter refused and barricaded
themselves, pulling out their mili-
tary Mausers in a menacing
manner. The deadlock lasted until
11.37 a.m. when the armed terror-
ists finally surrendered.

Shops Closed

All shops in the vicinity were
closed during the tension. The
streets were almost deserted ex-
cept for a few curious spectators.
According to official sources the
situation was not so grave. An
Italian patrol was said to have
found a group of armed men on
Jessfield Road, which is in the
Italian defense sector, and sur-
rounded them. The gang was dis-
armed and 26 taken into custody
indeed.

JUL 7 1935

Western District
Shootings

Armoured cars manned by members

it was understood, although no de-
finite solution has as yet been found.

sentations to the authorities con-

be taken whereby armed thugs would
not be permitted to come on to

territory.

ing, which is the latest in a series of

"North-China Daily News" learned
yesterday that the gunmen were not
connected with the "Ta Tao" authori-
ties nor with Mr. Wang Ching Wei's
bodyguard but that the gang consisted
of a large number of well-armed
criminals of the worst type, most of
whom have seen the Ward Road Gaol
from the inside on more than one
occasion and who are willing and
ready to do anything in their "line"
for the highest bidder.

Major Fujino

Expressing grave concern over

tain H. Smyth, Deputy Commis-
sioner of the S.M.P., yesterday

tion of the talks opened Sunday

ed that the Japanese Gendarmerie

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
JUL 3 1939

“Ta Tao” Gangsters
Fire at Policemen
Armoured Cars Patrol
Edinburgh Road; Strong
Protests by S.M.P.

A uniformed search party, con-
sisting of one foreign and three Chi-
nese members of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police, yesterday were saved
from almost certain death at the
hands of “Ta Tao” gangsters thanks
to the prompt arrival on the scene of
a party from Bubbling Well Police
Station. Some 20 shots were fired by
the gangsters notwithstanding the
large number of pedestrians on the
street at the time but the police did
not reply, not wishing to cause casual-
ties amongst innocent pedestrians.
This one-sided gun-battle, one of
the worst to have occurred here
during the past few months, com-
menced when five or six suspicious-
looking Chinese who were coming on
to Edinburgh Road from the Ts Yu
Pang alleyway on the west side of
the thoroughfare, refused to submit
to a search and dashed across the
Settlement street into an alleyway
on the other side from where, as-
sisted by additional gunmen, they
opened fire on the S.M.P. men.

Take Cover

The latter, not wishing to cause
casualties, took cover, two in a rice
shop on the East side of Edinburgh
Road and two others in a pawnshop
on the other side and Bubbling
Well police station was informed
of what had occurred by telephone.
This was at 3.40 p.m. and ten min-
utes later, the heavily armed police
party arrived, whereupon the gun-
men, who were all armed with heavy
Mauser pistols, ran into their alley-
way where the police could not
follow as that territory is not under
their jurisdiction.
Prior to the arrival of the police
party however, the gunmen who had
seen the two policemen—one a for-
eigner—take cover in the rice shop,
ran around the building and returned
to Edinburgh Road in front of the
shop from where they fired twice at
point blank range at the policemen
but fortunately without injuring
them.
At this point, the police party
arrived, whereupon the gunmen
withdrew. The heavily armed police-
men remained on the scene for about
half-an-hour, subsequently withdraw-
ing whilst investigations were im-
mediately commenced. No cartridge
cases were found on the scene as the
gunmen picked them up prior to
leaving. Captain H. M. Smyth,
District Commissioner and Mr. A. H.
Samson, Assistant Commissioner,
arrived on the scene soon afterwards,
subsequently returning to Bubbling
Well station. Energetic representa-
tions were addressed to the local
officer in charge of the Gendarmerie
in that sector and a conference,
between this official and high officers
of the S.M.P. has been called for
9.30 a.m. today.

Armoured Cars Patrol

Two armoured cars belonging to
the S.V.C. have been detailed for
patrol duty along Edinburgh Road
in the meantime and they are man-
ned by two members of the Machine-
gun Company, S.V.C. and two for-
eign police officers who are armed
with Thompson sub-machine-guns. The
military vehicles have been detailed
for duty there in order to afford
uniformed police officers the neces-
sary cover, it being felt that when
they patrol on foot or on motor-cycles
their uniforms make them easy tar-
gets, whilst the gangsters, dressed in
plain clothes, may easily hide amongst
pedestrians.

Although it was believed that the
Shanghai Municipal Police were
aware of the affiliations of the gun-
men who participated in yesterday's
attack on the police, no information
was available on the subject.

While certain quarters believed that
the gunmen were members of gangs
protecting gambling dens in that
district, other quarters stated that
they were members of Mr. Wang
Ching Wei's bodyguard, which with
a strength of 106 well-armed and
well-trained men, are living in that
vicinity. They have modern equip-
ment including steelvests and are
well trained and carefully chosen
men. No substantiation for this
statement could be obtained last night
however.

Strong Stand Taken

It was believed that the Shanghai
Municipal Police would take a strong
stand at this morning's conference in
view of the fact that shoot-ups in that
district have been frequent of late
and endanger the lives of Settlement
residents. It was believed that the
"Ta Tao" authorities would be asked
to carefully guard all alleyways lead-
ing on to Settlement streets in an
attempt to prevent armed men from
leaving "Ta Tao Territory."

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JUL 3 1939
S.M.P. Search Party Is
Fired Upon By Gangsters
While On Edinburgh Road
Group Of Chinese Refuse To Submit To Search,
But Run Off Into Alleyway And Fire At
Police At Almost Point Blank Range
NO ONE INJURED; GUNMEN ESCAPE
AS REINFORCEMENTS ARRIVE
The situation of utter lawlessness prevailing in western
outside areas was again revealed yesterday afternoon when a
Shanghai Municipal Police search party, operating along
Edinburgh Road between Great Western and Yu Yuen Roads,
was fired on by a group of gunmen from a Chinese controlled
alleyway abutting on the Municipal road.
About nine or ten shots were fired at the police search
party, which consisted of a foreign probationary sergeant and
three Chinese constables. Some of the shots were fired at
almost point blank range from Mauser pistols, and it was only
by taking cover in shops along the street that the police officers
escaped unharmed. In their turn, the police, first, were not
able to return the gunmen's fire for fear of hitting some innocent
pedestrians, and later because they were placed at a disadvant-
age.
The gunmen, of whom there were
about 15 in number, only retreated
deep into the City Government con-
trolled territory after reinforce-
ments had arrived from the Bub-
bling Well Police Station. The
shooting occurred at about 3.40 p.m.
and the area has remained quiet
since then. The police remained on
the scene for about half an hour,
but as the gunmen did not return,
the police left.
Later in the evening, the Shang-
hai Municipal Police called upon the
Armoured Car Company, S.V.C., to
supply two of their vehicles to
patrol the area where the shooting
had occurred. The Armoured Cars
remained on patrol throughout the
evening and night, being driven by
a member of the Armoured Car
Company and carrying one gunner
of the Company in addition to two
officers of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, each with a machine-gun, in
order to be prepared to deal with
any eventualities.
Strong Representations
Strong representations were
made by the Shanghai Municipal
Police yesterday afternoon to the
officer in charge of the Japanese
Gendarmerie in that area in con-
nection with the firing upon the
S.M.P. It is understood that a
conference between high ranking
officers of the S.M.P. and the
Japanese Gendarmerie is to be held
this morning, when the S.M.P.
officers will request the Japanese
to act immediately to curb the
movement of armed desperadoes in
the City Government controlled
territory.
It will undoubtedly be stressed
that as these lawless elements only
use the Municipal roads on rare
occasions, it is up to the Japanese
Gendarmerie and the City Govern-
ment Police to round up the various
gangs operating from and along the
City Government controlled territory.
After the shooting yesterday the
police could find no tangible
evidence as to who the gangsters
were. The garments they left
behind the

Refuse Search

The latest incident along the
extra-Settlement roads occurred
when some suspicious looking
Chinese coming out of an alleyway
on the west side of Edinburgh Road,
between Great Western and Yu
Yuen Roads, refused to be searched
by the S.M.P. search party, compos-
ed of one foreign and three Chinese
officers. These five or six Chinese,
instead, ran across to an alleyway
on the east side of the road and,
from there opened fire on the police
officers.

The gunmen were joined by about
ten more men, all of whom drew
their pistols. Being completely
outnumbered and fearing to hit
pedestrians, the Search Party was
forced to take cover. The foreign
officer and one Chinese stepped into
a rice shop on the east side of the
road, while the other two Chinese
constables took cover in a pawn-
shop on the opposite side.

Apparently out for blood, two of
the gunmen ran around the back-
of the rice shop and, coming out on
to Edinburgh Road again, fired two
shots at almost point blank range at
the men taking cover in the rice
shop. By then the two other Chinese
constables in the pawn shop had
called up the Bubbling Well Police
Station and a party of police rush-
ed to the scene. Immediately upon
the arrival of the police reinforce-
ment, the gangsters retreated into
Chinese territory, but were not fol-
lowed by the S.M.P. officers, as
the area is outside of their juris-
diction. The police party remained
on the scene till about 4.30 p.m. and
then left.

Precautionary measures were in-
stituted in that area by putting
armoured cars on patrol along the
section of the road involved.

Military Informed

The British military authorities
were informed of the shooting, it
having occurred in their defence
sector, but as the shooting was not
against Gendarmerie or City Gov-
ernment Police, but against ordin-
ary loafers and gangsters, the
matter was left entirely in the
hands of the Shanghai Municipal
Police.

Subject: ATTEMPT TO KIDNAP ONE YANG CHAO, AN
EMPLOYEE OF THE TASS NEWS AGENCY

About 10 a.m. December 22, 1939, a Russian staff member of
the Tass Soviet News Agency informed C. I. Emelianoff
by telephone that a Chinese translator of the agency had
been made the object of an unsuccessful attempt at kid-
napping by two persons who claimed they were detectives
from the Political Branch of the French Police.

C.I. Emelianoff requested his informer to make
an official complaint to the Police. This was sent to
the Political Section at 12.15 p.m. (See copy attached).

About 3 p.m. M. CHARIKOFF, "Soviet Consular
Representative" in Shanghai, telephoned C.I. Emelianoff
to secure information on this affair. He was told that
the French Police desired to interrogate Yang Chao
(楊潮), the victim of the attempted kidnapping.
Mr. CHARIKOFF stated that this person would come to the
Political Branch at 4.30 p.m. the same day in company with
Mr. BERNOFF, the manager of the Tass Agency.

Me Tseung (丁默邨), head of the Social Department

to kidnap Yang Chao to interrogate him on the activities

Subject. Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army - Tang Wei Ming (唐惠民),
a principal promoter of the organization, suspended from duty.

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

E

It is reported that Tang Wei Ming, one of the
principal promoters of the Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army was recently suspended from duty for
excessive use of authority.

Tang, it is said, was sent to Nanking in
October, 1939, by the Central Kuomintang organized
by the Wang Ching Wei clique to participate in the
celebration of the 1st Anniversary of the formation
of the Reformed Government and at the same time to
negotiate for the buying over of a certain
pacification army of the Reformed Government.
However, while Tang was in the middle of negotiations,
Wang Ching Wei gave instructions that the scheme be
abandoned. On account of the fact that a considerable
sum of money had already been spent and that the
negotiations were proceeding smoothly, Tang decided
to ignore the order and carried on the task which
culminated in the conclusion of an agreement with
the commander of the army.

On his return to Shanghai he explained the
situation to Wang Ching Wei but met with a sharp
rebuff from the latter for exceeding his authority
and was subsequently suspended from duty. He is said
to be confined in 76 Jessfield Road at present.

Subject. Friction between the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army and the "Shanghai City Government Police Bureau" over payment of "protection fees" by gambling houses &c.
Made by D.S.I. Mac Adie Forwarded by C. [Signature]

It is reported that a certain amount of friction now exists between members of the various sections of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army and officers of the "Shanghai City Government Police Bureau" stationed in the Western District, O.C.L., over the collection of remuneration from gambling dens, opium hongs and factories situated in the enclaves. The members of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army are receiving almost the whole of the remuneration which is paid out by these enterprises in the form of "protection fees." The "Shanghai City Government Police Bureau" officers contend that they should be entitled to at least half of the money forthcoming from this source on the grounds that they bear the chief responsibility in the maintenance of peace and order in the area.

As a result of this jealousy it is said that members of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army, while travelling in the extra-Settlement roads after mid-night, have been halted on several occasions by members of the "Special Reserve Unit" of the "Shanghai City Government Police" and detained on the street until dawn despite their disclosing or producing proof of their identity.

Notice Issued by Inmates of House 76 Jessfield Road

The following notice, published by the inmates
of House No.76 Jessfield Road, appears in the "Central
China Daily News" to-day:-
Of late cases of unlawful interference with
factories, shops and residents in the Western District by
lawless elements who are making use of the name of this
office in the furtherance of their unlawful activities
such as extortion or forcible occupation of houses have
been reported.
The members of this office are all under
strict surveillance and control and are strictly forbidden
to engage in any unlawful activities. The public are
hereby requested to detain all such persons no matter who
they are or where or when such cases take place, and telephone
up immediately to No.22812 or No.22915, when officials
will at once be detailed to the place for investigation.
All offenders, no matter whether they are or are not members
of this office, will be handed over to the competent and
proper authorities to be severely dealt with. It is
sincerely hoped that public bodies in the Western District
will render us their co-operation so as to put a check
on lawlessness.
This notice is published for the information
of the public.

course of training covering a period of one month.

2. That after completing the course of training, the
members will be sent back to serve in the various
branch offices.

in which they undergo training at Headquarters. (These

Information from a reliable source is to the
effect that between 8 a.m. and 11 a.m. October 27, a
meeting took place in the Headquarters of the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army, 76 Jessfield Road, O.C.L.,
when a number of department chiefs and officers in
charge of branch offices of the Corps situated in the
extra-Settlement roads area attended. Li Shih Chung,
Assistant Director of the Corps, presided and suggested
that all the branch offices situated in the extra-
settlement roads area be abolished and the members
attached thereto be transferred to Headquarters. He
added that those who have no wish to comply with this
order and prefer to resign from the organization would
be permitted to do so only they had handed over their
firearms. A lengthy discussion then took place over
the possibility of insurrection by the members of the
corps on learning of the scheme, the majority of whom
are lawless elements in possession of their own firearms
and who joined the organization because of the monetary
benefits. It was eventually decided that in order to
eliminate such a possibility all the records of the
members of the various branch offices, including
photographs and guarantee bonds, which are kept in the
respective branch offices be submitted to Headquarters
that day.

At 4 p.m. the same day, another meeting was held

viewed him and requested him to afford whatever assistance
he possibly could.
At 3 p.m., Monday, August 7, Inspector Sung Liang Fu
telephoned D.S.I. Chang Yuen Ching, Bubblingwell and stated
that if Inspector Tabrum would visit 94 Jessfield Road, the
prisoner (i.e. informer) would be handed over.
At 3.30 p.m., 7-8-39. Inspector Tabrum and D.S.I.
Chang Yuen Ching went to 94 Jessfield Road where Inspector
Sung Liang Fu stated that the prisoner was still being held
at 76 Jessfield Road. He boarded the car and instructed the
chauffeur to proceed from 94 to 76 Jessfield Road and by a
newly constructed road which connects them at the rear.
Upon reaching the gate of the last address,
admittance was refused by three armed Chinese sentries who
advised us to go to the main entrance on Jessfield Road.
We did as instructed and were promptly admitted. We proceeded
along the drive from the gate to the house, passing armed
sentries spaced at intervals of five yards. It was noticed
that there were about seventy armed men on duty on the grounds,

Sheet No. 2.

Some of whom in addition to being armed with mauser pistols
had a Chinese execution sword secured to their backs.
We were conducted to a reception room on the ground floor
of the house. After a short wait, Lee S Ching entered and
promptly lectured us in the policy of Mr. Wang Ching Wei,
a part of which was to gain as many adherents as possible
and that the only way peace could be restored to China was
for all Chinese to become believers in the policy of Mr. Wang
Ching Wei. In his opinion, the British were responsible for
the non-recognition and in absence of co-operation with his
party which now had been established in Nanking, Sungkiang, Wusieh,
and other large towns in occupied territory. According to
one present named Wu, who was called a Captain. Lee was in
charge of the entire organisation.
Eventually Lee discussed the actions of his followers
to win support for Mr. Wang Ching Wei and the suppression of
the opposition. He admitted frankly that his men were
responsible for the outrages committed against a pro- Central
Government newspaper on 22-7-39 at Avenue Edward VII but state
that he did not instructed his men to take such drastic action
Lee S Ching stated that the Chinese editor of the newspaper
had been warned to desist from publishing anti-Wang Ching Wei
propaganda, but as the editor was receiving financial support
from the Chiang Kai Shek regime, he had refused to do so.
therefore, his (Lee's) men considered necessary to bring
pressure in an attempt to make the editor change his mind.
Lee S Ching stated that he had been informed by a British Ind.
highly placed in the Force, that eight men had been detailed
to tap his telephone. Further, that D.S.I. WU Ching Ho,

Sheet No. 3.

had been put in charge of these men by Mr. T. Robertson who
was not in any way sympathetic toward the Wang Ching Wei party
and that Mr. T. Robertson had reprimanded Mr. Tan for passing
the information concerning the tapping of the telephone.
Questioned concerning the informer (the reason for the
visit), Lee S Ching said, that this man was a follower of C.D.S.
Wong Ching Sung who frequently expressed his opposition to the
Wang Ching Wei party in the detective office (Chinese) at
Bubblingwell Station, also that the C.D.S. had a number of
informers in O.C.L. territory who report adversely on his (Lee's
activities. He emphasised that he would have C.D.S. Wong Ching
Sung executed. Lee continued concerning C.D.S. Wong Ching Sung
by stating that he had two junior detectives as bodyguards and
that he had rented a room in the Central Hotel. He concluded
by saying in earnest that Wong Ching Sung should be transferred
if his life was to be saved.
The informer was handed over to D.I. Tabrum at 6.20
p.m., 7-8-39. Before leaving the premises, Lee S Ching casually
took $100 from his pocket and threw it at the informer remarking
that it was for hospital expenses. The informer's physical
condition was bad; his body was covered with bruises as a result
of being subjected to the torture known as Lou Foo Tun (Tiger's
Bench). He could not walk properly. On the instruction of
Mr. Yorke, D.O. "B" the informer was sent to hospital for
treatment.
The informer stated that two reasons were given him
for his intended execution; (a) He was not a follower of Wang
Ching Wei and (b) He was an informer of C.D.S. Wong Ching Sung
P.S. Lee included in his statement that Doo Yueh Sung

Sheet No. 4.

now in Hongkong had been contacted and was coming to Shanghai
in the near future and would support the policy of the Wang
Ching Wei Party.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

D.O. "B".                          Detective Inspector

ARREST OF C.D.C. 279 BY ARMED MEMBERS
OF TIH SUH CHUNG (鐵血軍).
======================================

For the purpose of verifying an address given by
a suspect in a larceny case brought to the Bubbling Well
Station by C.P.O. 1365 at 6.15 a.m. June 22, 1939.
C.D.C. 279 was despatched by D.S. 252 Weeks to Lane 1421,
House 5, Yu Yuen Road.

The C.D.C. proceeded by station car and alighted
at the entrance to the alleyway. He was looking for
the number of the alleyway standing on the Yu Yuen Road
footpath when two male Chinese, who were standing at the
entrance to the alleyway suddenly threatened him with
mauser pistols. The detective thinking they were
highway robbers offered them money. The suspected
robbers pulled the detective into the alleyway and there
searched him and upon finding that he was armed accused
him of being a traitor. At this juncture the two
suspects were re-enforced by about 20 other armed men.
The C.D.C. was subjected to interrogation and then
marched away to a Chinese style house in the Zau Ka Yi
village situated between Edinburgh and Great Western
Roads.

At 8.05 a.m. June 22, Inspector Yao Kyia Kwei
received a telephone message from Lee Shih Chung (李石崇)
living at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road, C.C.L.

Misc.No.335/39.
1/2.

informing the Inspector that a detective attached to
Bubbling Well Station had been arrested by a gang of men
and he would effect the release of the detective as a
mistake had been made,
In consequence of this message D.I. Tabrum, Inspr.
Yao Kyin Kwei and D.S. Weeks promptly proceeded to Lane
95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
Upon arrival at the lane leading to this house,
the Police party noticed several armed men standing in
the alleyway. Evidently the Police party were expected
as the iron door leading to the compound of the house
was promptly opened to admit them.
Upon entering the compound, the Police were confron-
ted by about 30 men all armed with mauser pistols. The
gate-keeper was armed with a mauser fitted with an
automatic stock.
The Police party were escorted to a large room on
the ground-floor. They were received in a very friendly
manner by Lee Shih Chung who introduced the 10 or 12
men present, some of whom were armed. Included in these
introduced were Sung Tsocng Mei (沈忠美), Zee Wen Ocn
(徐文安), a Mr. Chu and one named Lee Yih Fei (李飛).
The last named, according to information of Bubbling
Well detectives was shot by Inspector Dudley and D.S.I.
Tilton when participating in an Armed Robbery at No.5

Misc.No.335/39.
1/3.

Fah Wah Sing Tsung off Rockhill Avenue, Misc.No.207/39
(BW) and later removed to Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh
Road in Lee Shih Chung's M/car. During the discussion
Lee Tih Fei openly admitted being shot three times
and showed the Police the scars on his body resulting
from the bullet wounds he received. He was shot twice
in the back and once in the buttocks.

Lee Shih Chung who was previously unknown to any
of the visiting Police is a man of small stature, aged
about 35/6. He claims to be the owner of a steamship
line and also the owner of a Native Bank on Kiukiang
Road. He is a loquacious talker and desires to give
the impression that he is a man of great power. In
response to many questions concerning himself and the
numerous armed men surrounding him, he stated in
principle, that he had was a man of such power that he
was not subject either to the rule of the Japanese
or members of the Shanghai City Government. He had
under him between 700 or 800 men, most of whom, he
stated had been recruited from the villages in the
Western Area of Shanghai. This organization, he
called the Tih Suh Chung (Iron Colour Corps) (鐵血軍
50 of whom act as bodyguards to himself.

Misco. No. 335/39.
1/4.

Questioned as to the expenses for the upkeep of
this organization, Lee stated they are at present
poorly supported but when they need funds he provides
them.

The object of this organization, Lee stated, is
to eliminate members of pro-Chinese assassination
groups. Lee even went so far as to say that C.D.C. 279 would have been executed if it had not have been for the
fact that he was able to establish his identity by virtue
of the fact that he had a S.M.P. Warrant Card and S.M.P.
pistol and was later proved to be a member of the S.M.P.

Lee proposed that his organization be accorded
friendly treatment by detectives at Bubbling Well
Station with whom he expressed a desire to co-operate
for the specific purpose of exterminating members of
pro-Chinese assassination groups. He further stated
that as Police at Bubbling Well Station were responsible
for law and order in territory under the jurisdiction
of the S.M.C. in the Western Area that he be afforded
all possible protection.

Lee concluded the discussion which had lasted more
than one hour by stating that within a month or two
from now Mr. Wang Ching Wei would probably come to
Shanghai and there would be peace and quietness in the
Western Area of Shanghai.

Misc.No. 335/39.
1/8.

During the discussion Sergeant Major Shida
entered the room, he was greeted in a friendly manner
by all. He left after a few minutes, not knowing the
reason for presence of the S.M.P. Lee stated as he was
not obliged to tell Sergeant Major Shida, whom he would
not inform of the incident.

Some of the men the Police saw and were introduced
to at Lee's residence were students between 20 and 25
years of age. Others were of the robber and loafer type.

The C.D.C. was handed over to D.I. Tabrum together
with his pistol and Warrant Card at about 10.15a.m.
With the exception of being scared the detective had
not been injured in anyway.

After returning to the Station, Inspector
Yamaguchi approached D.I. Tabrum and asked if there had
been any trouble at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
He explained that Sergeant Major Shida had just phoned
for information and stated that to approach this
particular house was very dangerous and, that he had
received instructions from a high authority to cause
the arrest of all unauthorized persons found in the
vicinity thereof.

Inspector Yamaguchi was told that Police went on
a friendly visit at the request of Lee Shih Chung.

D. I. Tabrum
Det. Inspector.

Made by....................and....................Forwarded by....................D.I. Crawford

On the morning of September 1, 1939, three
members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army
called at the Kan Kung (幹公) Primary School, 121
Brenan Road, O.O.L. (within perimeter) and demanded
that the school evacuate and hand over the premises to
the Corps for the accommodation of its members. This
school, which has a total of some 1,000 students,
refused to comply with the demand on the grounds that
the evacuation would cause the students to suspend their
studies at least for the present semester as the school
is not in a position to find other accommodation in such
a short period.

After negotiations with the Corps by Wu Tsung
Yuen (吳宗瑗), principal of the school, it was agreed
that the hall and the recreation ground instead of the
whole premises be taken over only.

On September 3, a number of workers employed by
the Corps visited the school and commenced taking
measurements for the construction on the recreation
ground of huts which, it is reported, will provide
accommodation for some 1,000 members of the Corps.

solicited the assistance of the attendance in connec-

assistance of journalists was always of first impor-

as Ting Muh Tsung and Li Shih Chung personally arranged
the dinner party.

Date August 26, 1939.
Subject Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

Tenants of three of the twenty houses in the
Hwa Tsung alleyway, Jessfield Road, who failed to
remove on August 24, as instructed by the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army at 76 Jessfield Road, were
ejected on the morning of August 25, 1939, by three
Chinese members of the corps who were each armed with
a Mauser pistol.

It is reported from a reliable source that some
2,000 men consisting chiefly of ex-guerrilla members
who hitherto operated in the suburbs of Shanghai have
been bought over by the corps and after reorganization,
will be despatched to the Western District of Shanghai.
The first batch of these men, numbering some 500, it
is reported, are due to arrive towards the end of
September and the houses in the Hwa Tsung alleyway
on reconditioning will be made into billets for those
people.

The members of the Special Service Corps of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army have given the people in the Western
District to know that garrison duties in the entire
Western District and its suburbs at present undertaken
by the Japanese Authorities will be handed over to
them in the near future.

21 AUG 1939
Translation of letter to Mr. Franklin,
Chairman of Council, from Tseu Yan-pei
(海佛周) and Ting Meh-pong (邦默丁).
Dated 17th August, 1939.
Address: No. 76, Jessfield Road.

Newspapers, etc,: Police attitude objected to.
The Chung'ing Government, under the forcible control
of Communists and semi-Communists, is now pursuing a perverse
policy tending to drive the Chinese people towards an
inextricable doom. All Chinese are deeply indignant about this.
To save our country, our Party and our people from the
present crisis, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Vice-Chairman of the
Kuomintang, has resolutely opposed Communism and advocated
peace. With the exception of Communists, all quarters have
expressed profound sympathy with the stand taken by Mr. Wang;
this fact, we trust, is also well-known to the Council Chairman.
The Council's Police Department, however, have adopted
an unjust, non-neutral, unfriendly and discriminating attitude
towards us, and have unreasonably oppressed us as if we were
their enemies. The following particulars may be pointed out
as proofs:
1. The S.M. Police have not only failed to prevent Chinese
language newspapers in the International Settlement from
opposing Mr. Wang Ching-wei and his views, and from frequently
publishing reports which are without any foundation, but have
afforded those papers careful protection with large parties of
heavily armed Detectives and Constables. This has caused
these newspapers to be more aggressive in the tone of their
editorials and to publish more untruthful news. This is the
first point.
2. Because the Police have not arrested all terrorists, but
have allowed them to take shelter in the Settlement, their
activities have recently much increased. The Police therefore
are guilty of negligence. This is the second point.

3. Under the direction of Mr. Robertson of the S.M. Police,
eight Chinese, working in three shifts, have been ordered to
pick up telephone messages to and from No. 76 Jessfield Road
throughout the day and night. This is the third point.
4. During the last half month armed police and cars mounted
with guns have been sent to keep a careful watch in the
neighbourhood of No. 76 Jessfield Road. Persons connected
with us have been subjected to searches. This is the fourth
point.
The above particulars are sufficient proofs that the S.M.
Police are unjust towards us and are not neutral. We know, however,
that the Chairman and his honorable country have always been
strictly impartial in their attitude and have a deep aversion
towards Communists. Will the Chairman please give careful attention
to the above points.
We beg to submit the following proposals for the Council's
consideration:
1. All armed detectives and policemen detailed to protect
various newspaper offices should be withdrawn, and the offices should
be warned not to attack in future the views advocated by Mr. Wang.
2. If the police officers are not promptly withdrawn, then
the newspaper offices must cease to attack the views and written
articles of Mr. Wang; if the newspapers refuse to comply, the
Council must withdraw police protection.
3. The Police Department should be instructed to effectively
suppress the activities of terrorists in the Settlement and to
refuse them shelter. As soon as any report is received from us,
the Police should do its utmost to have the persons concerned
apprehended so that terrorism may be completely eradicated. When
a terrorist is arrested, and there is sufficient evidence to prove
him to be such, he should be handed over to us to be dealt with.
If there is no evidence against him, a further investigation should
be conducted jointly by the Police and ourselves, and an arrangement
should be made as how to deal with the man; he should not be

-3-

released without our consent.

4. The Police to be instructed not to send men in future
to pick up telephone messages to and from house No. 76,
Jessfield Road, so that we may not be deprived of the freedom
of speech.

5. Armed police officers posted near premises No. 76,
Jessfield Road, should be withdrawn and persons having connexions
with us should not be searched.

The above mentioned proposals are very reasonable and
lawful. We hope that they will receive the Council's careful
consideration and will be duly adopted. Should our proposals
be adopted, we guarantee that hereafter no action will be taken
by us in the Settlement. If our proposals are rejected and
the Police officers are still to be used as tools for other
people, we shall not be responsible for the occurrence of
untoward incidents which may undermine the peace and good
order of the Settlement.

the same evening after representations had been made
by the Japanese Military Authorities.

Chief of Staff of the Corps, who was seen among those
taken away by the Italian Marines on August 3, appeared
at No.1081 Jessfield Road. According to him all the
members of the corps arrested by the Italian marines
had been released, hence the report on the release of
the members submitted on the morning of August 4.
It is reported, however, that at about 12 noon,
a small section of Italian marines called at No.1081
Jessfield Road and, after placing Zee Wen Oen and an

entrance of Jessfield Park on Brenan Road we were surrounded
by a number of men, all of whom were armed, for searching.
Nothing incriminating was found on our persons, but we were
all handcuffed and taken into a waiting car, licence number
unknown, to a HOUSE NO. 94, JESSFIELD ROAD, the premises of
the JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE. We were then taken into the
Interrogation Room and questioned by a Japanese Officer
through a Chinese Interpreter, in the presence of a dark fat
Chinese. The Interpreter stated that we were formerly members
of a group for the riddance of traitors and making
disturbances, for which reason we were arrested. The
Interpreter then asked us if we were the members of the
group in question. We answered in the negative. We were
detained there for a period of 3 weeks after beating up by

Subject Zao Ka Doo Merchants' Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road
- visited by executives of the "Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army"
Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford

At 9 a.m., on July 28, 1939, Sung Chung Mei
(孫志潔) and Wong Yung Ching, sectional chiefs
of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Cmintern and National Salvation Army,
with headquarters at No.6, Lane 95, Zuen Ching Li,
Edinburgh Road, called at the office of the Zao Ka
Doo Merchants' Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road.
They informed Zung Sien (陳選), Secretary of the
Union, who received them that as the house on Edinburgh
Road, in which their Iron and Blood Corps is situated
was inadequate, they were directed by their superiors
to request the use of the office of the Union. When
informed that the premises of the Union was private
property, the visitors appeared to be offended and
departed in a haughty manner saying that they would
move in with or without the consent of the Union.
Following the above visit, an urgent meeting
was called at which Ao Pah-daung (夏伯棠) presided
and the following resolutions were discussed and
passed :-
(1) That Kitaoka (北岡), Director of the Shanghai
City Government in the Western District, be
petitioned to instruct those people that the use
of the private property of the Union should not
be allowed.
(2) That Mang Kuo-bei (孟國培), nicknamed "Siau
Koo Pai" (小骨牌), proprietor of the Ding
Sung Tai (鼎順泰) Cigarette and Exchange
Shop, 1089 Jessfield Road, who is reputed to be
connected with the Special Service Corps on
Edinburgh Road, be requested to call on the
executive of the Corps to explain the views
of the Union.

The branch office of the Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army at House 6, Zeu Ching Li,
inside Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, O.O.L., has been
abolished; the members, some 70 in number, hitherto
accommodated therein have removed to the Headquarters
of the corps at No.76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L..
The abolition of the office, it is said, is due
to the fact that it has not been managed to the
satisfaction of the Japanese Military Authorities.
The latter consider that the members have not kept
their activities secret enough when carrying out
their work with the result that the Settlement autho-
rities have been able to gain a complete knowledge
of the organization and its workings.
After they had removed to House 76 Jessfield Road,
these members were instructed to hand over their fire-
arms to the corps for safe-keeping which was carried
out. The majority of these members brought their
own firearms when joining the organization, the guns
being their personal property. They were also warned
that in future they would be punished if seen carrying
pistols without permission from the corps headquarters.
It will be recalled that on the morning of July 28,
1939, Sung Chung Mei (孙忠谋) and Wong Yung Ching
(王荣庆), two executive staff members of the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern

REPORT

Subject. Further to:- Investigations made into the activities of thirteen
members of the "Special Service Corps" of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern & National Salvation Army", arrested by British Military.

Made by D. I. Glover Forwarded by Supt. Bennett

Sir,

The following is a brief resume of the cases in
which the arrested persons have been identified or
implicated :-

(1) 3rd, 6th & 10th accused

Murder & Attempted Murder (Cent. F.I.R. 2155/39)

This case concerns the armed attack made by
members of the above organisation at about 8.30 p.m.
22-7-39, on the premises of the "Chinese-American Daily
News", No. 160 Avenue Edward VII, which resulted in the
death of Mr. A.F. "Tug" Wilson (American) and thirteen
other casualties.

The 6th accused, who admits participation and
implicates the 3rd and 10th accused, was on the 7th March
1940 identified by an employee of the above newspaper.

Three of the pistols seized by British Military,
i.e. "Mauser" Pistols 892708, 1749, and "Astra" Pistol
No. 6396, on examination by the Arms Identification
Section, were found to have been used in this crime.

(2) 12th accused

Attempted Armed Robbery (Chengtu Rd. F.I.R.730/39)

At about 10.30 p.m. 23-5-39, a number of armed
men attempted to commit an armed robbery at House No. 69,
Lane No. 506, Taku Road, but on an alarm being raised,
decamped after firing one shot to intimidate the inmates.

The 12th accused was identified on the 7th March
1940 by a female servant employed at the above address.

Made by. H.I. Glover Forwarded by Supt. Bennett

Sir,

At about 9.30 a.m. February 27th 1940, a patrol
of the 2nd Bn: East Surrey Regiment observed two armed male
Chinese loitering in Crescent Avenue off Yu Yuen Road.
Following the arrest of these two men, a raid was carried
out on House No. 17, Jung Ka Lah (鄭家宅), West Tsu An
Bang (西諸安浜), off Yu Yuen Road, where eleven further
arrests were made and seven more pistols seized. All
thirteen men and the seized pistols were detained by

At the request of the British authorities,
D.J. Macadie of the Special Branch, S.M.P., questioned
the arrested men, with the result that it was ascertained
that they were members of the 3rd Section of the 2nd Coy.

a list of the names and particulars of the arrested

During the morning of the 1st March 1940, the
und rsigned and D.I. Crighton, acting on instructions
received, took over from the British Military the thirteen
arrested men for interrogation.
On these persons being fingerprinted it was
found that the undermentioned men had been previously
convicted :-
9th. Yang Tseng San (楊俊山) - "Illegal Detention" -
6 months imprisonment, suspended
for two years, 19-6-39 (B'W. 688/39).
13th. Sung Tseng Hai (宋正海) - "Highway Robbery" -
8 years imprisonment, 30-11-27
(H. E2036). Sentence reduced under
Government Amnesty - Released on
remission of sentence 4-3-33.
One other man, namely the 10th accused, An Sieu
San, had been charged with "Assault", on the 15-6-39, but
was found "Not Guilty" on being arraigned before the 1st
S.M.D.C. (B'Well 96174).
On being individually questioned, the thirteen
men admitted that they were members of the organisation
in question, under the immediate command of Major Lao
Bang Zung, who receives his instructions from the sub-
office of the Special Service Corps situated at No. 35
Edinburgh Road.
The were aware of the fact that these orders
usually emanated from either Woo Sz Pao (胡書保) or Li
Sz Chuen (李士全), Commanders of this organisation, with
Headquarters located at No. 76 Jessfield Road.

As the result of continuous interrogation
statements were finally obtained from the 10th accused
An Sieu on concerning three further cases, particulars
of which are given hereunder :-
After giving a brief resume of his life up to
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, he relates
how he enlisted in a patrol unit under the Commander-in-
Chief of the 3rd War Zone of the Chinese Nationalist
Army. Following the retreat on Nanking this particular
corps to which he was attached was reorganised and named
the "Rear Defence Orderly Staff" of the "Military Affairs
Committee". He remained with this unit until ordered to
Changsha, when owing to ill health he was granted sick
leave to proceed to Shanghai. Returning to this city in
May 1938 he took up residence at No. 1005 Brenan Road,
which he operated as a macaroni shop. On the 2nd August
1939, he became acquainted with Zau Bang Zung, Captain
of the 3rd Section of the 2nd Squad, Special Service
Section of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern &
National Salvation Army. On expressing a wish to join
this organisation he was taken to No. 35 Edinburgh Road,
where he was enlisted as a member of the Corps at a salary
of $45.00 including a subsistence allowance. On the 1st
September 1939, by order of one Yang Jih (楊傑),
Commander of the 2nd Squad, he was transferred to the 3rd
Section under the command of Zau Bang Zung, who had
established offices at No. 17 Sung Ka Zah (孫家宅),
Yu Yuen Road. At this address he was issued with an
imitation Browning auto: pistol No. 2715 and six rounds

I am a member of the 3rd Section, 2nd Squad of Wang
Ching Wei's Defence Corps.
        I was born at Tsang Tsong (張庄) Village to the
east of Chinchow Hsien, Hopei Province. At the age of 9 I
was admitted to a primary school in the village, where I
pursued my studies until I was 16 years old. I then assisted
my parents in farming. At the age of 22 I came to Shanghai
and lived at the home of my cousin An Sieu Foong (安秀峯),
who was a policeman attached to the Public Safety Bureau in
Nantao. After remaining there for about a week, I was taken
by my cousin to sit for an examination at the Public Safety
Bureau, which I passed and was subsequently appointed as a
policeman attached to the Public Safety Bureau Headquarters
at a monthly salary of $12.00. I was thus employed for
about 3 years, after which I obtained a position as Police
Constable No.695 of the French Police. I was then 25 years
old and my first assignment was to go on duty at Ave. Petain
Police Station and later I was transferred to Ave. Joffre
Station. After completing about two years' service, I applied
for leave to return to my native country due to the death of
my father. I was delayed 4 days when coming back to Shanghai
as the boat on which I sailed encountered a typhoon at sea.
As a result of this, I was immediately dismissed from the
French Police. I remained unemployed for about a month, after
which I joined the Anti-piracy Guard of the China Merchants
Steam Navigation Co. and was despatched for duty aboard the
S.S. "Hai Lee". My pay for this job was $16.00 per mensem.

(2)

I ceased to work there after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937. I then enlisted in the Patrol Unit under
the Commander-in-chief of the 3rd War Zone of the Nationalist
Army. Following our retreat to Nanking the troops were re-
organised to be known as the Rear Defence Orderly Staff of the
Military Affairs Committee. After our troops moved further
into Changsha, I suddenly commenced to spit blood and was
therefore granted sick leave to return to Shanghai. It was
then during the month of May 1938. I took up residence at No.
1005 Brenan Road, where I operated a "machine made" macaroni
business. On the 2-8-39, Zau Bang Zung (趙程), Captain
of the 3rd Section of Wang Ching Wei's Defence Corps, took me
to No.35 Edinburgh Road, where I was introduced to join as a
member of the Corps at a monthly pay of $45.00 including food
allowance. On the 1-9-39, by order of Commander Yang Jih (楊傑)
of the 2nd Squad, I was transferred to the 3rd Section under
the leadership of Captain Zau Bang Zung, with offices at No.
17 Sung Ka Zah, off Crescent Avenue. The personnel of our staff
are as follows:-

One Captain : Zau Bang Zung (趙鵬程)
Two Section : Zung Zih Tsu(2nd accused)
Chiefs (郭 碧 芝)
Lieu Dien Hwa(not arrested)
(劉 殿 華)

Eleven Executive Members.

One Clerk : Zing Yee Ming (1st accused)
(秦 義 民)
One Coolie : Sung Tsung Hai (13th accused)
(孫 正 海)

Three Cooks (Not arrested).

I was issued with a pistol No.2715 and 6 rounds of
ammunition.

(3)

At about 7 p.m. one day during September 1939
(15.9.39) Captain Zau gave orders at our office that we should
go out on a special errand and after assigning Zung Zah Ts (2nd
accused), Ying Shih Tsoo (4th accused), Tsang Kyung Nyoh (6th
accused), Ngah Ts Bing (11th accused), Chah Zih Kwang (not
arrested), Tseu Tih Fu (not arrested) and myself to the job,
stated that we could follow Section Chief Aung, who was cognizer
of the nature of our work. Armed with my pistol, I left with
the six others, who were all armed with Mauser pistols. We
proceeded on foot along Yu Yuen Road, and turned east to
Edinburgh Road, north of Kinnear Road, east of Jessfield Road,
and north to Connaught Road, where we stopped at the mouth of
Sing Kong Li alleyway. Before reaching the place Zung Zah Ts
told us that he was instructed by Captain Zau to take us to the
intersection of Jessfield and Connaught Roads with the object
of robbing Chinese policemen of their pistols. Presently we
saw three Chinese Policemen standing together at the entrance
to Sing Kong Li alleyway, whereupon we went forward and whilst
Chah Zih Kwang and Tseu Tih Foo pointed their Mauser pistols
at the policemen, Ying Shih Tsoo and Ngah Ts Bing took away
the pistols from two of them by cutting off the string attached
to the pistols with a 3 inch knife which they both carried. The
remaining policeman, however, succeeded in making good his

Hoh Tsoong Un, 6th accused Tsang Kyung Ngoh, 8th accused

31 MAR. 1940
COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE

TRANSLATION

In connection with your circular in favour of the
Peace Movement, it appears that your association is in
support of the Leader and is closely interested in the
national affairs. Such attitude on your part is deemed
highly beneficial to the Party and to the State. The
Chungking Government, however, has not yet awakened from
its dream and is making a desperate struggle by resorting
to mean threats in an endeavour to muzzle the press and
frustrate the Peace Movement. It is believed that your
association already understands these intrigues and therefore
no change is likely in your attitude.

Nevertheless, we send you this letter in view
of the possibility that unruly elements will take the
opportunity of chances furthering undesirable activities,
and that certain persons may be tricked owing to misconception.
If your attitude proves inconsistent trouble may follow, and
not only you will be despised by the public, but will be
severely punished as it is the duty of this Corps to prevent
any one from openly conducting activities against the Peace
Movement. Do not say that no previous warning was given.

Under the pretext of guarding factories in the extra-
Settlement roads area in the western District from acts

service corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern

industrial concerns in the enclaves in turn, warning them
to apply to the two offices in question for registration.

November 29, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News:

FACTORIES BEING FORCED TO REGISTER

Shortly after 10 a.m. yesterday, a reporter of
the Hsin Kwang News Agency (新光社) secured the following
information:-
A "Factory Owners' Registration Office" is
operating in Lane No.110 Ni Wei Road (倪家路) off Brenan
Road in the Western District. Its officials are armed.
On the night of November 27, they carried off certain
articles of furniture etc. from several shops in the
vicinity and took them to Lane No.110 Ni Wei Road for
their own use.
Upon learning this, the reporter made a personal
inspection at the place and his investigation confirmed
the above report.
At about 5 p.m. information was received from
foreign factories to the effect that a number of factories
in the vicinity of Kong Ka Kiao (康家桥) were being forced
to apply for registration certificates which would be
issued at $6 each. Should a factory owner refuse to
register, certain measures would be taken to deal with him.
It is learned that the honorary chief of the
office is one Chang (张), with one Vai (萬) as chief.

Subject. Pro-Wang Ching Wei Clique - to secure dominance over various Chinese Circles in Shanghai.
Made by...D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien, Forwarded by... C Crawford.

It is reported that the Wang Ching Wei Clique is accelerating its efforts to secure dominance over various local Chinese circles in the hope that when the proposed government under Wang Ching Wei is inaugurated (the inauguration was originally scheduled for October 10 and is now said to have been postponed to November 1) it will have the support of these circles and will receive greetings from them. In connection with these movements, the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army has organized four sections namely:-

1. Labour Movement Section in charge of Chang Kuh Chong (張克昌), a committee member of the local Postal Workers Union.
2. Merchant Movement Section in charge of Pan San Sing (潘省三), ex-conductor of the Asia Club, 65 Gordon Road.
3. Student Movement Section in charge of Chen Chi Zung (陳濟成), ex-principal of the Shanghai Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road.
4. Woman Circles Section in charge of (1) Miss Kyung Kwang Mei (金光楣), ex-proctor of the Hwai Kiu Middle School for Girls and head of a rival clique among the faculty of the school engaged in a dispute over the appointment of a new principal in March 1939. She is at present the principal of the Chien Shu Middle School situated at No. 537 Weihaiwei Road.

Date September 17, 1939.
Subject Disarming of police constables in Western District, U.O.L.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie

On September 15, three Shanghai Municipal Police
constables were robbed of their service pistols
on Jessfield Road by a number of armed plain-clothes
men while on September 16 a further two constables
were similarly disarmed on Brenan Road.

It is learned that the robberies are the work
of members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army attached to the branch office of the organization
at 1081 Jessfield Road, U.O.L., and were carried out
with a view to:-
1. embarrassing and obstructing the S.M.P. authorities.
2. convincing members of the Chinese Branch that the
S.M.P. is powerless in the extra-Settlement roads
area in the Western District, thereby undermining
the morale of the former.

It is reported that these attacks will continue
until definite measures have been laid down in settle-
ment of the dispute over the question of policing the
extra-Settlement roads area in the Western District.

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S. I.

On the afternoon of July 15, 1939, with the assistance of Police constables of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, members of the Special Service Corps, 7C Jessfield Road, of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army" (中國國民黨反共救國軍), a pro-Japanese armed corps at No. 6 Lane 95, Edinburgh Road distributed in the Western District, O.O.L., pamphlets and coloured paper slips of an anti-communist and pro-Wang Ching Wei nature purporting to have emanated from the Three People's Principles Anti-Communist Youths' Corps (三民主義反共青年團). The pamphlets contain an epistle addressed to Chinese youths urging them to support Wang Ching Wei and his peace policy of national salvation, while on the paper slips anti-communist and pro-Wang Ching Wei slogans appear.

Copies of similar pamphlets were also found on the afternoon of July 15, at the corner of Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads.

Attached to this report is a specimen of the pamphlet and the coloured paper slips in question together with translation.

AN EPISTLE TO THE YOUTHS OF THE WHOLE NATION

Dear youthful Comrades :

For the existence and independence of the nation,
we have been fighting a sacred war of resistance for the
past two years. When we look back into history, we
cannot but recollect that prior to the August 13 Incident
the communists in China were about to meet defeat and
that the Kuomintang had fulfilled its mission of unifying
China preparatory to reconstructing a new nation. Reali-
zing their own precarious position and in order to save
themselves, the communists played upon the patriotic
sentiments of the people and rallied them under their
banner in the name of a war of resistance against Japan.
When the July 7 Incident broke, the door of peaceful
settlement was blocked by the exaggerated propaganda of
the communists thus frustrating the policy of national
reconstruction. The Kuomintang was compelled to
embark upon a war of resistance as a last resort in saving
the party and the nation.

The lesson gained in the sanguinary war of two years
has amply proved that China is incapable of extinction, and
this is realized by Japan. We feel that the time has
arrived for China and Japan to commence peace negotiations
on condition that the two nations be placed on an equal
footing.

Since his advocation of peace in Chungking, Mr. Wang
Ching Wei has candidly stressed the following point :-

"The purpose of a state is to maintain its

(2)
existence and independence whether at war
or peace. We should not shrink from
war should war be inevitable, and we
should not refuse negotiation for peace
when peace is possible. When peace is
to be concluded it should depend on whether
it adversely affects the existence and
independence of China."
This is the unfailing truth, which should serve as
a guide to the continued existence of this nation.
But the communists are against peace; they would rather
see China continue in her suicidal path of war for an
indefinite period than have her abandon the resurrected
Red Army and its political dominance which they obtained
under the plea of a war of resistance.
We fully realize that the time is now ripe for
peace and that the "principles of rapprochement, joint
anti-comintern and economic cooperation" as advocated
by Mr. Wang Ching Wei should form the basis for Sino-
Japanese cooperation for the establishment of permanent
peace in the Orient.
We firmly support the policy of national salvation
through peace; we reaffirm our faith in the Three People's
Principles; and we assert that we will concentrate our
strength with the will of the Fascist spirit and endeavour
to bring about national salvation and national reconstruction.
Youthful Comrades! Unite!
Support the peace policy of national salvation as
stated by Mr. Wang!
Oppose the Government's policy of continuing the
war of resistance!

(3)

Elucidate the teachings of the late Tsung Li
Sun Yat Sen !

Down with the Communist Party, the running dog
of the Third Internationale!

Long Live the Republic of China!

The Three People's Principles
Youths' Corps.

Dated July 15.

statements are attached hereto.

in various local printing presses, including the Commercial

My name is Wong Sao Ching alias Wong Pei Shing (王必兴),
aged 28, native of Taichow, Kompo, married, residing at 61
Woo Huh Faung (和合坊 ), Avenue Joffre.

At the age of 15, I came from my native home to Shanghai
and worked as a coolie on various wharfs in Nantao. After
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in
August, 1937, I left Nantao and joined the Roosevelt Terminal
as a coolie (No.395).

At the beginning of February, 1939, one Nien Shing
(嚴鑫 ) was appointed by the management of the Roosevelt
Terminal as a foreman coolie; he later left and joined some
organization.

In the middle of April 1939, Nien Shing told me while
I was working on the wharf that he could secure a far better
job for me and asked if I would accept it. On being question-
ed as to the nature of the employment, Nien stated that
"Central" (中央) (National Government) was recruiting
secret agents and should I join I would have a very hopeful
future. He also told me that the pay would be about $30.00
per mensem.

On May 6, 1939, Nien took me to the Van Saung Tea Shop
(萬商茶樓 ), junction of Fokien and Canton Roads, and Tsang
Tien Zai (張天在 ), another coolie of the Roosevelt Terminal
who also expressed his willingness to work as a secret agent,
accompanied us. There we met Loh Yao Ling (陸耀令 ) and
Tsang Ding Sung (張挺生 ) who, we were told, were members of
the secret service and would take charge of a section in which

From a usually reliable source, it has been learned
that the two Chinese who were rumoured to have been kid-
napped by certain unknown persons from the King Kong
Restaurant, Rue Wagner, in the evening of June 22, 1939,
are actually two section chiefs of the secret intelligence
service of the Chungking Government operating in Shanghai.
One of the two persons kidnapped is reported to be named
Hsu Yien (許 燕) but the name of the other is not known.
After having been taken away from the restaurant, they
were said to have been sent to 76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.
and were interviewed there by Ting Luh Tsung (丁默村),
formerly Chief of the Military Investigation Section of
Military Affairs Commission of the National Government
and at present Director of the "Special Service Corps
of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army" (中國國民黨剷共救國軍別動隊), a pro-
Japanese and pro-Wang Ching Wei organization with head-
quarters at House 10, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, O.O.L..
They were warned by Ting to leave Shanghai as soon as
possible and were released separately the same evening.
Ting Luh Tsung is said to know the majority of the
senior secret service agents of the National Government
in Shanghai for most of them were under his control when
he was Chief of the Investigation Section of the Military
Affairs Commission. Ting is a staunch supporter of
Wang Ching Wei and, following the latter, changed his
allegiance from the National Government and is now work-
ing for the Japanese.
His arrival in Shanghai (about the end of April, 1939)
has been the cause of a general reorganization in the
secret service of the National Government operating in
